Net-cash parent funds 99acres's growth
Large stakes in Eternal (Zomato) and PB Fintech

Competition from Housing.com, MagicBricks and NoBroker
Reported profit swings with investee valuations

anarock.name: ANAROCK

notes: Privately held; founded by Anuj Puri

notes: Venture-backed unicorn
Earns from subscriptions, home loans and home services

squareYards.name: Square Yards
squareYards.role: Brokerage, property portal, mortgage and interiors platform

notes: Privately held; operates in India and the Middle East
Not listed - no market data

lt.name: Larsen & Toubro

strengths: Strongest balance sheet and execution record in Indian construction
Wins the largest and most complex building contracts
risks: Buildings is a small part of a much larger infrastructure, energy and defence group - not separately disclosed here

ahluwalia.name: Ahluwalia Contracts (India)
ahluwalia.role: Building contractor for hospitals, institutions, offices and residential towers

risks: Profitability is still young; Q2 is seasonally weak
IFRS vs Indian GAAP profit gaps confuse comparisons

iciciLombard.name: ICICI Lombard General Insurance
iciciLombard.role: India's largest private general insurer; health (retail and group) is one of its biggest lines
strengths: Large hospital network and bank distribution
Diversified book cushions health-claims cycles
risks: Health is a part of a broad general-insurance business
Group health is price-competitive with thin margins

newIndia.name: New India Assurance
newIndia.role: India's largest general insurer (government-owned); health is its largest line, much of it group and government business
strengths: Largest health premium book in India by volume
Government ownership and pan-India reach
risks: Group and government health often runs at loss-making claims ratios
Weak underwriting profitability historically

mediAssist.name: Medi Assist Healthcare Services
mediAssist.role: India's largest third-party administrator (TPA) - processes cashless and reimbursement claims for insurers and employers
strengths: Scale leader in TPA; bought Paramount TPA (Jul 2025) and moved its business into its own TPA from Feb 2026
Revenue grows with group health premiums under management
Technology platform sold to insurers
risks: Insurers bringing claims processing in-house
Fee pressure; regulatory changes to TPA roles

careHealth.name: Care Health Insurance
careHealth.role: Standalone health insurer, a subsidiary of listed Religare Enterprises
strengths: One of the top standalone health insurers by retail premium
risks: Unlisted itself; parent Religare saw a control change in 2025
notes: Subsidiary of Religare Enterprises (listed separately)
No listed market data for the insurer

policyBazaar.name: PB Fintech (Policybazaar)
policyBazaar.role: India's largest online insurance marketplace - a major channel for new retail health policies - and, through PB Healthcare, a new entrant building hospitals in NCR
strengths: Largest share of online retail health insurance sales
PB Healthcare raised capital (2025) to build an insurer-aligned hospital network
risks: Hospitals are a long, capital-heavy bet outside its core
Regulation of insurance commissions

practo.name: Practo
practo.role: Unlisted doctor-discovery, teleconsult and clinic/hospital software platform
strengths: Large base of doctors and patients using its booking platform
risks: Unlisted; long path to profit
notes: Bengaluru
No listed market data

pharmEasy.name: PharmEasy (API Holdings)
pharmEasy.role: Unlisted e-pharmacy and B2B medicine platform; majority owner of listed Thyrocare
strengths: Among the largest digital pharmacy platforms
risks: Unlisted; heavy losses and a 2023 down-round rights issue
notes: Private; recapitalised with Manipal group support in 2023
No listed market data

tata1mg.name: Tata 1mg
tata1mg.role: Unlisted e-pharmacy, lab-test and teleconsult platform of Tata Digital
strengths: Tata group balance sheet and Tata Neu ecosystem
risks: Unlisted; loss-making
notes: Subsidiary of Tata Digital
No listed market data

sbiFunds.name: SBI Funds Management (SBI Mutual Fund)
sbiFunds.role: India's largest fund house by assets - SBI's joint venture with Amundi, selling through SBI's branch network as well as distributors
strengths: Largest AMC by AUM, with SBI's 22,000-plus branches as a captive channel
Listed on 21 Jul 2026 after an IPO subscribed ~42 times (offer for sale by SBI and Amundi)
Leads in EPFO-linked ETFs and new SIF launches (Magnum SIF)
risks: Large share of low-fee ETF and debt assets lowers its revenue yield
Depends on SBI's network - a state-bank parent with its own priorities
Fell below its issue price within weeks of listing

iciciAmc.name: ICICI Prudential Asset Management
iciciAmc.role: No. 2 fund house, strong in equity and hybrid funds; ICICI Bank's joint venture with Prudential plc
strengths: Large equity and hybrid book earns a higher fee yield than debt-heavy peers
ICICI Bank's branch and digital reach
Listed in Dec 2025 through Prudential plc's stake sale
risks: Sensitive to equity-market falls given its equity tilt
SEBI's April 2026 expense rules trim fee yields across the industry

hdfcAmc.name: HDFC Asset Management
hdfcAmc.role: Third-largest fund house and the longest-listed pure AMC (2018), with a large equity and distributor-led book
strengths: Equity-heavy AUM with an ~11% share of industry quarterly AUM (Q2 FY27)
High operating margins and a long record of high payouts
Broad network of independent distributors plus HDFC Bank
risks: Q2 FY27 profit grew only ~4% as tax costs rose and yields fell
Fee yield erosion from telescopic expense ratios as funds grow
Competition from new low-cost AMCs

nipponAmc.name: Nippon Life India Asset Management
nipponAmc.role: Large fund house owned by Japan's Nippon Life, India's biggest ETF manager and strong with retail SIP investors in smaller towns
strengths: Largest ETF franchise in India (Nippon India ETFs) - wins passive flows
Strong retail and B-30 (smaller-city) presence
Offshore and alternatives businesses add to the mutual-fund core
risks: ETF assets earn thin fees, diluting yield
Small-cap fund concentration makes flows sensitive to small-cap sentiment

abslAmc.name: Aditya Birla Sun Life AMC
abslAmc.role: Mid-sized fund house from the Aditya Birla group (with Sun Life), historically strong in debt funds
strengths: Debt and fixed-income depth, plus a growing passive and alternatives book
Group distribution through Aditya Birla Capital
risks: Has lost equity market share over several years
Debt-heavy mix lowers fee yield and swings with debt outflows (heavy in Mar and Sep 2026)

utiAmc.name: UTI Asset Management
utiAmc.role: India's oldest fund house (from the Unit Trust of India), with large EPFO/NPS pension mandates and index funds
strengths: Runs a big share of NPS pension money (UTI Pension Fund) and large ETFs
Long-standing brand in smaller towns
risks: Losing equity market share; much AUM is low-fee passive or pension
No promoter - ownership spread across SBI, LIC, Bank of Baroda, PNB and T. Rowe Price

canaraRobeco.name: Canara Robeco Asset Management
canaraRobeco.role: Mid-sized, equity-focused fund house owned by Canara Bank and Orix's Robeco
strengths: Equity-heavy mix earns a high fee yield for its size
Canara Bank's branch network for distribution
Listed in Oct 2025
risks: Small market share, so it lacks scale economies of the top five
Concentrated in a few large equity schemes

jioFin.name: Jio Financial Services
jioFin.role: Reliance group's financial-services arm; its 50:50 Jio BlackRock venture launched a low-cost mutual fund in 2025 and plans broking
strengths: Jio BlackRock pairs BlackRock's index and risk tools with the reach of Jio's tens of crores of users
Built over ₹15,000 Cr of fund assets within months of launch (Mar 2026)
risks: Still small in a market where scale decides margins
Price-led entry mainly hurts incumbents' passive and debt fees - its own profits are years away

prudent.name: Prudent Corporate Advisory Services
prudent.role: One of India's largest independent mutual-fund distribution platforms, serving tens of thousands of distributors with tech and back office
strengths: Equity-heavy, long-held SIP assets earn sticky trail commissions
Strong in smaller towns where advice-led selling dominates
Growing insurance and stock-broking cross-sell
risks: Trail income depends on AMC commissions, which SEBI's expense rules squeeze
Direct plans and apps take self-directed investors

njIndia.name: NJ India Invest
njIndia.role: Unlisted - India's largest independent mutual-fund distribution network, which also runs NJ Mutual Fund
strengths: Largest distributor network by AUM among non-bank distributors
risks: Unlisted - no public market data
notes: Surat-based, promoter-owned
Launched its own AMC (NJ Mutual Fund) in 2021
No listed market data

pbFintech.name: PB Fintech (PolicyBazaar, Paisabazaar)
pbFintech.role: India's largest online insurance marketplace (PolicyBazaar) and a credit marketplace (Paisabazaar) - the distribution layer for protection products
strengths: Dominant share of online health and term-insurance sales, with renewals building a recurring base
Turned profitable as renewal income and the offline-assisted model scaled
PB Health (hospital network) and UAE business extend the platform
risks: IRDAI commission and expense-of-management rules can cap payouts
Heavy marketing spend; PB Health investments dilute near-term margins
Insurers building their own digital channels

groww.name: Groww (Billionbrains Garage Ventures)
groww.role: India's largest broker by NSE active clients, built as a mobile-first app for stocks, F&O, mutual funds and margin funding; also runs Groww AMC
strengths: Over a quarter of NSE active clients; kept adding clients in Q1 FY27 while the industry lost them
Largest platform for direct mutual-fund SIPs, so it gains from SIP growth as well as trading
Q1 FY27 revenue +66% YoY with very high margins for a broker
risks: F&O is still a big share of revenue - exposed to SEBI and STT changes
Listed only in Nov 2025 - a short public record
Direct-plan mutual funds earn it little; it monetises through broking and lending

angelOne.name: Angel One
angelOne.role: Large listed discount broker (about 4 crore clients, Sep 2026) with F&O-heavy volumes, margin funding and a new AMC and wealth arm
strengths: Third-largest by NSE active clients (~14.7% in Sep 2026, just behind Zerodha) with strong reach outside the metros
Q2 FY27 profit +58% YoY; client funding book averaged ~₹7,450 Cr in the quarter and closed at a record ~₹8,210 Cr
Diversifying into mutual funds (Angel One AMC), wealth and credit distribution
risks: Most revenue still comes from F&O orders - directly hit by SEBI curbs and the STT hike
Retail equity turnover share slipped ~0.5 pt QoQ to ~19.7% in Q2 FY27
Gross client additions fell year on year in Sep 2026

zerodha.name: Zerodha
zerodha.role: Unlisted - India's pioneering discount broker and one of the two largest by active clients; owns Zerodha Fund House (with Smallcase)
strengths: Highly profitable, bootstrapped and debt-free; sets the price benchmark for the industry
risks: Unlisted - no public market data; F&O curbs cut its revenue sharply in FY26
notes: Bengaluru-based, founder-owned (Kamath brothers)
Has said it has no plans to list
No listed market data

motilal.name: Motilal Oswal Financial Services
motilal.role: Diversified capital-markets group: full-service and discount broking, wealth (private wealth), asset management (Motilal Oswal AMC, PMS/AIF) and investment banking
strengths: Exposure across almost every layer - broking, wealth, AMC, IB
Motilal Oswal AMC's mid/small-cap funds have gathered large flows
Large treasury book of own fund investments
risks: Treasury gains (mark-to-market) swing reported profit with markets
F&O curbs hit the broking arm
Fund performance concentrated in a few momentum-style schemes

fivePaisa.name: 5paisa Capital
fivePaisa.role: Small listed discount broker (spun out of the IIFL group) focused on low-cost retail trading
strengths: Pure-play on discount broking - high operating leverage if volumes return
risks: Losing share to larger apps; revenue has fallen since the F&O curbs
Small scale in a price war

iiflCapital.name: IIFL Capital Services
iiflCapital.role: Full-service broker, institutional equities house and investment bank (formerly IIFL Securities)
strengths: Regular IPO lead manager and institutional research franchise
Retail broking plus margin funding and distribution
risks: Both IB fees and broking volumes are cyclical
Lower SEBI caps on fund brokerage reduce institutional commissions

kotak.name: Kotak Mahindra Bank
kotak.role: Private bank whose subsidiaries include Kotak Securities (a top-five broker), Kotak Mahindra Capital (a leading IPO banker) and Kotak Mahindra AMC
strengths: Kotak Mahindra Capital leads many of the largest Indian IPOs and blocks
Kotak Securities and Kotak Neo give it a large broking base
risks: Capital-markets businesses are a minority of a bank-led group - lending drives the figures

three60One.name: 360 ONE WAM
three60One.role: India's largest listed private-wealth manager for ultra-rich families, with an alternatives-led asset-management arm
strengths: Total AUM of ~₹6.7L Cr (Mar 2026), with recurring (ARR) assets now the larger share of revenue
Bought UBS's India wealth business and B&K Securities to add clients and institutional broking
Alternatives (AIF, private credit) earn higher fees than mutual funds
risks: Wealthy-client assets are concentrated - team or client exits move AUM
Transactional and carry income falls in weak markets

nuvama.name: Nuvama Wealth Management
nuvama.role: Wealth manager (formerly Edelweiss Wealth, controlled by PAG) with asset services (custody, clearing), institutional equities and private markets
strengths: Asset-services arm clears and custodies for foreign portfolio investors - a market-plumbing earner too
Strong institutional equities and IB franchise
Fast-growing private and affluent wealth businesses
risks: Was a clearing member for Jane Street - a reminder that capital-markets income can concentrate in a few large traders
Cyclical IB and transactional wealth income

anandRathi.name: Anand Rathi Wealth
anandRathi.role: Mutual-fund-led wealth manager for high-net-worth families, earning mainly from distribution trails and structured products
strengths: AUM of ~₹93,000 Cr (Mar 2026) growing fast on equity MF and structured products
Very high return on capital for an asset-light model
risks: Structured-product (market-linked debenture) income is sensitive to SEBI rules and markets
Distribution trails depend on AMC commission rates
Rich valuation (see the figures)

jmFinancial.name: JM Financial
jmFinancial.role: Leading domestic investment bank (equity capital markets, M&A) with institutional broking, private wealth and a shrinking lending book
strengths: Consistently near the top of Indian equity league tables
Simplifying the group after exiting much of its wholesale lending
risks: SEBI's 2024 order restricting its public debt-issue lead-manager work (over a bond-IPO lapse) shows the conduct risk
Lending-book legacy weighs on returns

equirus.name: Equirus Capital
equirus.role: Unlisted mid-market investment bank and institutional broker - a frequent lead manager on mid-cap IPOs and QIPs
strengths: Active in mid-cap equity raises; also runs wealth and broking arms
risks: Unlisted - no public market data
notes: Ahmedabad/Mumbai-based
Not listed (checked Nov 2026)
No listed market data

nse.name: National Stock Exchange of India (NSE)
nse.role: India's dominant stock exchange and the world's largest derivatives exchange by contracts; owns NSE Clearing, Nifty indices, data and co-location businesses
strengths: ~93% of cash-market turnover and nearly all equity futures (FY26, per RHP)
Very high operating margins on a mostly fixed cost base
Listed on BSE on 24 Sep 2026 after a ~₹22,562 Cr offer for sale - no promoter, widely held
risks: Equity options are its largest revenue line - SEBI curbs and BSE's Sensex options cut its premium share from ~97% (FY24) to ~68% (Q1 FY27)
FY26 profit fell on lower volumes and a co-location settlement provision
Regulatory and governance scrutiny that comes with being the market's core

bse.name: BSE
bse.role: Asia's oldest exchange, now a real No. 2 in index options after relaunching Sensex weekly options; also runs StAR MF (mutual-fund order platform) and India INX at GIFT City
strengths: Took roughly a third of options premium turnover in 2026 from near zero in 2023
StAR MF handles a large share of mutual-fund distributor transactions
Fixed Thursday weekly expiry gives it a distinct trading day
risks: Earnings concentrated in one product - Sensex options on expiry days
RBI's tighter bank-guarantee rules for brokers (Jul 2026) may cap options turnover
Any SEBI move to cut weekly expiries again hits it hardest

mcx.name: Multi Commodity Exchange of India (MCX)
mcx.role: India's commodity derivatives exchange, with near-total share in gold, silver, crude and base-metal futures and options
strengths: Near-monopoly in commodity derivatives
Bullion options drove record volumes - Q1 FY27 options turnover more than tripled YoY
New technology platform (since 2023) supports product launches
risks: Volumes swing with gold and silver volatility
SEBI may extend F&O-style curbs to commodity options as retail piles in
NSE and BSE compete in commodities

crisil.name: CRISIL
crisil.role: India's largest rating agency, majority-owned by S&P Global, with global research, benchmarking and risk-analytics businesses
strengths: Research and analytics for global banks earn steadier, dollar-linked income
Leading share in bond and bank-loan ratings
risks: Domestic ratings dip when bond issuance falls (Apr-Jun 2026)
Global research depends on investment banks' outsourcing budgets

icra.name: ICRA
icra.role: Rating agency majority-owned by Moody's, with a large analytics and outsourcing arm serving Moody's
strengths: Debt-free with a large cash pile
Moody's-linked analytics work adds steady fee income
risks: Smaller domestic market share than CRISIL
Rating revenue tied to the bond and bank-loan cycle

care.name: CARE Ratings
care.role: Third-largest Indian rating agency, independent of a global parent, expanding into ESG, risk and Africa
strengths: Pure play on Indian ratings growth with operating leverage
Growing ESG, advisory and international businesses
risks: Past governance lapses (SEBI action after IL&FS) still shape perception
No global parent to feed analytics work

indiaRatings.name: India Ratings & Research (Fitch)
indiaRatings.role: Unlisted - Fitch Group's Indian rating agency, a top-four player in bond and bank-loan ratings
strengths: Fitch backing and strong share in infrastructure and structured finance ratings
risks: Unlisted - no public market data
notes: Wholly owned by Fitch Group
No listed market data

cdsl.name: Central Depository Services (CDSL)
cdsl.role: India's larger depository by accounts (~19 crore, Aug 2026) - the default for discount brokers' retail clients
strengths: Holds about four in five demat accounts - every new retail investor adds to its base
Annual issuer fees, KYC (CVL) and e-voting give income beyond trading
Debt-free, with high margins
risks: Debit and transaction fees fall when retail trading slows
Rising technology and regulatory costs kept margins under pressure in FY26
SEBI fee decisions set its prices

nsdl.name: National Securities Depository (NSDL)
nsdl.role: India's first depository, holding most of the market's value through institutional and custodian accounts; also runs NSDL Payments Bank
strengths: Custody value several times CDSL's - the depository of choice for institutions and FPIs
Listed on BSE in Aug 2025; long-standing role in PAN, tax and e-governance services
risks: Fewer retail accounts, so it gains less from new investors
Payments bank is low-margin and dilutes returns

cams.name: Computer Age Management Services (CAMS)
cams.role: Largest mutual-fund registrar (RTA), servicing about two-thirds of industry AUM (~₹58L Cr, Q2 FY27), plus KYC, payments, insurance and alternatives services
strengths: Long contracts with most large AMCs (HDFC, ICICI Prudential, SBI, Nippon) - switching is rare
Grows with AUM and SIP transactions without needing capital
Building non-MF lines: CAMSPay, KRA, AIF and insurance repositories
risks: Telescopic pricing - yield falls as AUM grows; renewals bring price cuts
Market share slipped slightly in Q2 FY27
Stock fell on results despite profit growth - growth is slowing to mid-teens

kfin.name: KFin Technologies
kfin.role: Second mutual-fund registrar (about a third of AUM) and India's largest issuer registrar for company shares, with international fund-admin clients
strengths: Services many of the newer AMCs, so it tends to win new entrants
Largest share of corporate registry and IPO allotment work
International fund administration (Ascent Fund Services) adds growth
risks: Overseas acquisitions dilute margins while they integrate
Same telescopic pricing pressure as CAMS
Corporate registry income depends on IPO activity

kec.name: KEC International
kec.role: RPG group EPC major and one of the world's largest transmission-tower builders; T&D is about three-fifths of its order book, alongside civil, railways and cables
strengths: Order book including L1 bids passed ₹40,000 Cr in Jun 2026, with power T&D ~62% of the unexecuted book
Long track record in Middle East (Saudi Arabia, UAE), Africa and the Americas, plus own tower and cable plants
Power T&D was 57% of FY27 order inflow so far - the core business is growing again
risks: Q1 FY27 profit fell ~42% on flat revenue - margins in non-T&D segments and legacy contracts drag
Fixed-price contracts exposed to steel and zinc prices
High working capital and debt for an EPC company

kpil.name: Kalpataru Projects International
kpil.role: EPC group (merged with JMC) with T&D as its largest business, plus buildings, water, railways and oil & gas; owns Linjemontage (Sweden) and Fasttel (Brazil)
strengths: Record order book of ₹66,607 Cr at end-Jun 2026
Wide international T&D footprint (Nordics, Latin America, Middle East, Africa)
Q1 FY27 profit rose ~45% as margins recovered
risks: Diversified EPC - T&D growth is diluted by other segments
Past losses at subsidiaries (Fasttel, road BOOT assets) and high working capital
Commodity and labour costs on fixed-price jobs

transrail.name: Transrail Lighting
transrail.role: Transmission EPC company that also makes its own towers, conductors and poles; listed in Dec 2024
strengths: FY26 order inflow above ₹8,500 Cr; power T&D is ~90% of the order book
Backward-integrated: tower, conductor and pole plants plus EPC
Tripling tower capacity to ~1.96 lakh tonnes a year (company plan)
risks: Smaller and newer to public markets than KEC and Kalpataru
Africa and Middle East projects carry country and payment risk
Working capital and bank-guarantee needs rise with the order book

lt.name: Larsen & Toubro
lt.role: India's largest EPC group; its Power Transmission & Distribution business builds substations, lines and grid projects in India and the Gulf (also in the energy sector for generation EPC)
strengths: Among the largest T&D EPC players globally, with big Middle East grid orders (Saudi Arabia, UAE)
Balance sheet and execution scale few rivals match
Can bid for HVDC civil and 765 kV packages
risks: T&D is one division of a conglomerate - small share of group earnings
Middle East concentration in large orders
Selective bidding means it does not chase every Indian TBCB EPC job

skipper.name: Skipper
skipper.role: Kolkata-based maker of transmission towers, monopoles and telecom structures that also does T&D EPC and runs a PVC-pipe business
strengths: One of India's largest tower makers with a growing EPC arm
Large orders from POWERGRID and overseas utilities
Adding tower and pole capacity
risks: Thin engineering margins and steel-price exposure
High working capital and debt
Pipes business adds volatility

bajel.name: Bajel Projects
bajel.role: Bajaj group's power transmission and distribution EPC company, demerged from Bajaj Electricals in 2023, with its own tower plant
strengths: Focused T&D EPC business with Bajaj group backing
Bidding for 765 kV and international work to scale up
risks: Small, with thin and volatile margins while older low-margin contracts run off
Order inflow is lumpy and competition from bigger EPC firms is intense

apar.name: Apar Industries
apar.role: India's largest conductor maker and a major cable and specialty-oil company; makes HTLS, copper and OPGW conductors and sells heavily overseas (also in data-centre and solar sectors)
strengths: Conductor order book of ₹10,190 Cr at Jun 2026, with exports 56.8%
Premium products (HTLS, copper conductors, reconductoring) about half of conductor revenue in Q1 FY27
Approvals from US data-centre operators for its cables
risks: Conductor volumes fell ~7% in Q1 FY27 even as revenue rose
US revenue fell in Q1 FY27 amid tariff uncertainty
Aluminium and copper price swings

sterliteElectric.name: Sterlite Electric (formerly Sterlite Power's products business)
sterliteElectric.role: Unlisted maker of overhead conductors, OPGW and EHV cables, split from the Resonia transmission developer in 2025
strengths: About 15% share of India's conductor market by value (FY25, company)
Strong in HTLS reconductoring and OPGW
risks: Unlisted - no public market data
Has filed draft IPO papers; listing timing unclear
notes: The products half of the former Sterlite Power group
No listed market data

guptaPower.name: Gupta Power Infrastructure
guptaPower.role: Unlisted Odisha-based maker of conductors, cables and wires
strengths: Large conductor capacity in eastern India serving utilities
risks: Unlisted - no public market data
notes: Odisha-based, promoter-owned
No listed market data

diamondPower.name: Diamond Power Infrastructure
diamondPower.role: Gujarat conductor and power-cable maker revived after insolvency by the GSEC group
strengths: Restarted conductor and cable lines with large orders from private transmission developers
Turnaround story with capacity already built
risks: Short track record since the insolvency resolution
Customer concentration and commodity exposure

karamtara.name: Karamtara Engineering
karamtara.role: Maker of transmission-line hardware, fasteners and tower parts, and of solar mounting structures (also in the energy and solar sectors)
strengths: Leading Indian supplier of line hardware and fittings to global transmission EPC firms
Exports to many countries; tower and hardware capacity under one roof
risks: Revenue tied to EPC customers' project timing
Steel and zinc price exposure

kei.name: KEI Industries
kei.role: Cable maker with one of India's largest EHV (up to 400 kV) cable businesses, plus HT/LT cable and wires (also in real estate and data-centre sectors)
strengths: Among the few Indian makers of 220-400 kV EHV cable; new Sanand (Gujarat) plant adds capacity
Strong institutional and export channels
risks: EHV is a minority of revenue; building wire competition is intense
Copper price swings
Capex ramp-up at Sanand

polycab.name: Polycab India
polycab.role: India's largest wires and cables maker, expanding into EHV cable and taking power-distribution and BharatNet EPC work (also in real estate and data-centre sectors)
strengths: Scale leader in cables with capacity to enter EHV
Large distribution network and export growth
risks: Transmission-grade EHV is still small for Polycab
EPC projects carry lower margins

univCables.name: Universal Cables
univCables.role: MP Birla group maker of EHV and HV power cables (up to 400 kV) and capacitors, Satna (MP)
strengths: Long-standing EHV cable maker approved by utilities
Group holding in Birla Corporation adds asset backing
risks: Small scale versus KEI and Polycab
Thin margins and project-linked revenue

genus.name: Genus Power Infrastructures
genus.role: India's largest smart-meter maker and an AMISP for discoms under RDSS (AMISP arm co-owned with GIC)
strengths: Executable order book of ~₹24,000 Cr at Jun 2026 (~₹25,200 Cr at Mar 2026), mostly AMISP contracts
Revenue grew ~45% in Q1 FY27
risks: RDSS installs are behind plan; any extension or slowdown delays revenue
AMISP model needs heavy capital and depends on discom payments
Receivables and working capital rise with installs

hpl.name: HPL Electric & Power
hpl.role: Meter and switchgear maker supplying smart meters to AMISPs and discoms, plus lighting and wires
strengths: Large meter capacity and RDSS orders from AMISPs
Also makes switchgear for distribution
risks: Thin margins and high working capital
Depends on AMISPs' order timing

technoE.name: Techno Electric & Engineering
technoE.role: Substation and transmission EPC company that became a smart-meter AMISP and is building data centres
strengths: Net-cash balance sheet and long substation EPC track record
AMISP contracts add a recurring-revenue stream
risks: AMISP execution and discom payment risk
Moving into data centres spreads management focus

intelliSmart.name: IntelliSmart Infrastructure
intelliSmart.role: Unlisted AMISP joint venture of EESL and NIIF, among the largest smart-meter rollouts in India
strengths: State backing (EESL) plus NIIF capital
risks: Unlisted - no public market data
notes: EESL-NIIF joint venture
No listed market data

hitachiEnergy.name: Hitachi Energy India
hitachiEnergy.role: Indian arm of Hitachi Energy (ex-ABB Power Grids): power transformers, HVDC, GIS, grid automation and power quality - the broadest grid-equipment maker in India (also in the data-centre sector)
strengths: Record order backlog of ₹32,222 Cr at 30 Jun 2026
HVDC technology partner for Khavda-Nagpur (with BHEL) and AESL's Rajasthan link
Revenue up ~69% and profit more than doubled in Q1 FY27; new transformer factory at Karjan (Gujarat)
risks: Very rich valuation - see the figures
HVDC orders are lumpy; Q1 FY27 intake fell after a large HVDC order a year earlier
Execution risk on several large fixed-price projects at once

gevtd.name: GE Vernova T&D India
gevtd.role: Indian arm of GE Vernova's grid business: power transformers, GIS, HVDC and grid automation
strengths: Won the ±800 kV, 6 GW Barmer-II to South Kalamb HVDC terminals from POWERGRID (Sep 2026) as lowest bidder
Transformer and GIS factories with growing export orders
Margins have expanded sharply since FY24
risks: Q1 FY27 order inflow was 30% lower year on year
Rich valuation - see the figures
Parent-driven export allocation and royalties

taril.name: Transformers & Rectifiers (India)
taril.role: Ahmedabad maker of power transformers up to 1,200 kV, furnace and rectifier transformers and reactors (also in the data-centre sector)
strengths: Expanding capacity from ~40,000 to ~75,000 MVA with new Changodar and Moraiya lines in FY27 (company)
Strong utility order book
risks: Execution on a large capacity jump
CRGO and copper costs on fixed-price orders
Rich valuation - see the figures

siemensEnergy.name: Siemens Energy India
siemensEnergy.role: Siemens Energy's Indian arm, demerged from Siemens Ltd and listed in Jun 2025: power transformers, HVDC, switchgear and turbines (also in the energy sector)
strengths: Approved ~₹2,060 Cr in Feb 2026 to add ~30,000 MVA of large power transformer capacity
Access to the parent's HVDC and grid technology
Exposed to both grid and generation capex
risks: Short listed history as a separate company
Rich valuation - see the figures
Capacity addition timing

cgPower.name: CG Power and Industrial Solutions
cgPower.role: Murugappa group maker of power transformers, switchgear and industrial motors, also building an OSAT chip plant (also in railways, data-centre and semiconductor sectors)
strengths: Power systems segment has a large order book and is adding transformer capacity
Strong balance sheet under Murugappa ownership
risks: Grid is one segment next to motors, railways and semiconductors
Rich valuation - see the figures

voltamp.name: Voltamp Transformers
voltamp.role: Vadodara maker of power and distribution transformers up to 220 kV, mostly for industrial and utility customers
strengths: Net-cash, high-return transformer maker with a conservative balance sheet
Strong brand with industrial and EPC buyers
risks: Limited exposure to 400 kV+ utility units
Cautious on capacity expansion while rivals add aggressively

shilchar.name: Shilchar Technologies
shilchar.role: Gujarat maker of power and distribution transformers with a large export business
strengths: Exports were ~48% of FY26 sales; capacity ~7,500 MVA
New unit due by Apr 2027 (company)
risks: US order intake hit by tariff uncertainty in FY26
Small company - single-site and customer concentration

atlanta.name: Atlanta Electricals
atlanta.role: Gujarat (Anand) maker of power, auto and inverter-duty transformers for utilities and renewable plants; listed Sep 2025
strengths: Strong in transformers for solar and wind plants and state utilities
Adding capacity after its IPO
risks: Short listed history
Customer concentration in state utilities and renewable developers

meil.name: Mangal Electrical Industries
meil.role: Jaipur company that processes CRGO steel into transformer laminations and cores, and makes transformers and does substation EPC; listed Aug 2025
strengths: CRGO processing gives it a hand in the tightest input in the chain
Integrated from laminations to transformers and EPC
risks: Short listed history and small scale
CRGO price and supply swings flow straight to margins
Rajasthan utility concentration

qpower.name: Quality Power Electrical Equipments
qpower.role: Sangli maker of reactors, HVDC and FACTS components and transformers for grid operators worldwide; listed Feb 2025
strengths: Niche in HVDC and FACTS components few Indian companies make
Exports to many countries; acquired Mehru Electrical to add instrument transformers
risks: Small company with lumpy, export-led orders
Rich valuation - see the figures

bhel.name: Bharat Heavy Electricals
bhel.role: State engineering major; HVDC consortium partner with Hitachi Energy, plus power transformers and substations (also in energy, railways and naval sectors)
strengths: Partner on India's ±800 kV HVDC terminals (Khavda-Nagpur for POWERGRID; Rajasthan for AESL)
Bhopal and Jhansi transformer plants and long utility relationships
risks: Transmission is small next to its thermal-power order book
History of slow execution and weak margins

siemens.name: Siemens
siemens.role: Siemens Ltd after the 2025 energy demerger: smart infrastructure (GIS, switchgear, substation automation), digital industries and mobility (also in the railways sector)
strengths: Strong in medium-voltage switchgear, substation automation and data-centre power
Parent technology and brand
risks: High-voltage grid equipment moved to Siemens Energy India in the demerger
Rich valuation - see the figures

abb.name: ABB India
abb.role: Medium- and low-voltage switchgear, distribution automation, drives and robotics (ABB's high-voltage grid business is now Hitachi Energy) (also in data-centre and railways sectors)
strengths: Leader in MV switchgear and distribution automation for utilities, data centres and industry
Net-cash balance sheet
risks: Little high-voltage transmission exposure
Rich valuation - see the figures

schneider.name: Schneider Electric Infrastructure
schneider.role: Schneider's listed Indian arm making distribution transformers, MV switchgear and grid automation (also in the data-centre sector)
strengths: Distribution transformers and switchgear for utilities and data centres
Turned around from losses to steady profits
risks: Distribution-level more than transmission exposure
Parent royalties and transfer pricing

hindalco.name: Hindalco Industries
hindalco.role: Aditya Birla aluminium and copper major: supplies aluminium rod for conductors and copper rod for windings and cables (also in Nifty 50, electronics and critical-minerals sectors)
strengths: Integrated aluminium plus India's largest custom copper smelter (Dahej)
Grid metals demand grows with transmission and cable capex
risks: Grid is a small slice of a global metals and Novelis business
LME prices and copper smelting charges drive earnings

vaml.name: Vedanta Aluminium Metal
vaml.role: India's largest aluminium producer (Jharsuguda, BALCO), demerged from Vedanta and listed on 15 Jun 2026; a major supplier of aluminium wire rod to conductor makers
strengths: Largest wire-rod supplier in India - conductors are a core end-market
Plans to roughly double smelting capacity (company)
risks: Listed only since Jun 2026 - short history as a separate company
Vedanta group debt and governance overhang
Aluminium price and power cost swings

nalco.name: National Aluminium Company (NALCO)
nalco.role: State aluminium and alumina producer selling wire rods and EC-grade metal to conductor makers (also in the critical-minerals sector)
strengths: Low-cost integrated bauxite-alumina-aluminium chain
Wire rod sales tie it to conductor demand
risks: Grid is a small share of sales; alumina prices drive earnings
State ownership limits capital allocation choices

hindcopper.name: Hindustan Copper
hindcopper.role: State-owned, India's only integrated copper miner - copper for windings and cables starts here (also in the critical-minerals sector)
strengths: Closest listed play on copper prices that grid and cable demand lift
risks: Small output; most Indian copper comes from imported concentrate
Earnings swing with the copper price

jswSteel.name: JSW Steel
jswSteel.role: Steel major whose 50:50 JV with JFE Steel (JSW JFE Electrical Steel) is India's only CRGO producer (also in Nifty 50 and real-estate sectors)
strengths: JV is expanding CRGO from 50,000 to 3.5 lakh tonnes a year (Nashik + Vijayanagar) from FY28, ~₹5,845 Cr capex
The JV's anti-dumping complaint (DGTR probe, Jun 2026) could raise CRGO import prices
risks: CRGO is tiny next to JSW's flat-steel business
Expansion timing and JFE technology transfer

powerGrid.name: Power Grid Corporation of India
powerGrid.role: State transmission utility owning most of India's inter-state grid; winner of the largest share of TBCB projects (also in Nifty 50)
strengths: Works in hand of ~₹1.75L Cr at Jun 2026, ~83% TBCB; bidding pipeline over ₹1.19L Cr
FY27 capex guided at ~₹37,000 Cr; capitalisation tripled year on year in Q1 FY27
Regulated assets earn a CERC-set return on equity
risks: TBCB projects earn lower returns than older regulated assets
Equipment lead times delay commissioning
Ladakh HVDC redesign and other flagship delays

adaniEnSol.name: Adani Energy Solutions
adaniEnSol.role: India's largest private transmission company, a Mumbai discom and an AMISP smart-meter business
strengths: 29,739 ckm network at Sep 2026, with an under-construction pipeline worth ~₹87,000 Cr (Q2 FY27)
Smart-meter order book of 24.6 million meters (~₹29,500 Cr revenue potential)
Led FY26 ISTS-TBCB awards by tariff share; Rajasthan HVDC link with BHEL-Hitachi Energy
risks: High leverage to fund a large under-construction book
Adani group governance overhang (US indictment of group executives, Nov 2024)
Smart-meter execution and discom payment risk

tataPower.name: Tata Power
tataPower.role: Integrated power company with Mumbai transmission, the Powerlinks JV, TBCB wins and Odisha/Delhi discoms (also in energy, solar and EV sectors)
strengths: Wins TBCB transmission projects and runs regulated Mumbai transmission
Discoms give it distribution and smart-meter exposure
risks: Transmission is a small slice next to generation and solar manufacturing
Large capex across many businesses

indigrid.name: IndiGrid (India Grid Trust)
indigrid.role: India's first power-transmission InvIT, sponsored by KKR, owning inter-state lines, substations, solar and battery assets
strengths: AUM of ₹34,041 Cr at Jun 2026; FY27 distribution guidance of ₹16.48 per unit
Sponsor EnerGrid builds projects (₹5,800 Cr of Himachal LOIs) for IndiGrid to buy later
risks: Net debt at ~58.5% of AUM; sensitive to interest rates
Acquisition-led growth needs fresh equity

pgInvit.name: PowerGrid Infrastructure Investment Trust
pgInvit.role: POWERGRID-sponsored InvIT owning five inter-state transmission projects
strengths: Low leverage and high-availability, POWERGRID-run assets
Steady distributions from TBCB tariffs
risks: No growth pipeline beyond the sponsor's choice to sell more assets
Fixed tariffs fall in real terms; unit price tracks interest rates

resonia.name: Resonia (formerly Sterlite Power's transmission business)
resonia.role: Unlisted private transmission developer that builds TBCB projects and sells finished ones to InvITs
strengths: 20 projects spanning ~11,500 ckm; won Kurnool IV REZ (Telangana) in Jun 2026
risks: Unlisted - no public market data
notes: Earlier sponsored IndiGrid and sold it assets
No listed market data

iex.name: Indian Energy Exchange
iex.role: India's largest power exchange, with the dominant share of day-ahead, real-time and green power trading
strengths: Near-monopoly share of exchange volumes with very high margins and no debt
More transmission and more renewables raise short-term trading
risks: CERC's market coupling would pool all exchanges' bids and erode its liquidity advantage - APTEL (Feb 2026) and the Supreme Court (Jul-Aug 2026) declined to stop it
Regulatory price caps and fee pressure

ptc.name: PTC India
ptc.role: India's largest power trader, buying and selling power across states and with neighbouring countries
strengths: Cross-border trade with Nepal, Bhutan and Bangladesh
Debt-light trading model with a high dividend payout
risks: Thin trading margins
Governance issues at its lending arm PTC India Financial Services

rec.name: REC
rec.role: State lender to power utilities and a nodal agency for RDSS; its REC Power Development & Consultancy arm runs TBCB bids and incubates project SPVs
strengths: Funds and designs a large share of the transmission pipeline
Government-backed borrowing costs
risks: Exposure to weak state discoms
Transmission is a minority of its loan book

pfc.name: Power Finance Corporation
pfc.role: State power lender and REC's parent; its PFC Consulting arm is a bid-process coordinator for ISTS TBCB projects
strengths: Largest power-sector lender; earns from both loans and bid-process fees
Holds a controlling stake in REC
risks: Concentrated exposure to state utilities and private gencos
Transmission is a minority of its loans

gridIndia.name: Grid Controller of India (Grid-India)
gridIndia.role: Unlisted state system operator that schedules and dispatches power on the national grid; proposed market-coupling operator
strengths: Named Market Coupling Operator in CERC's Apr 2026 draft
risks: Unlisted - no public market data
notes: Government-owned; formerly POSOCO
No listed market data

eternal.name: Eternal (Zomato, Blinkit)
eternal.role: Parent of Zomato (food delivery), Blinkit (quick commerce, the category leader), District (going-out) and Hyperpure (supplies to restaurants)
strengths: Blinkit's NOV grew ~79% to ~₹20,940 Cr in Q2 FY27 with positive adjusted EBITDA - now larger than food delivery
Food delivery is profitable (adjusted EBITDA ~5.5% of NOV in Q2 FY27) and funds expansion
Blinkit fulfils most orders from own inventory, lifting margin per order
Strong cash position from its 2024 QIP
risks: Flipkart Minutes and Amazon Now discounting could slow Blinkit's margin gains
Leadership change: Deepinder Goyal stepped down as group CEO in Feb 2026 (Blinkit's Albinder Dhindsa took over)
Group net profit is small relative to order value, so earnings are sensitive to small margin moves
Gig-worker contribution and rider-cost rules

swiggy.name: Swiggy
swiggy.role: No. 2 food-delivery app and owner of Instamart (quick commerce), plus Dineout, SteppinOut and Scenes
strengths: Food delivery is profitable and growing high-teens %
Raised ~₹10,000 Cr in a Dec 2025 QIP and ~₹2,400 Cr from selling its Rapido stake - a large cash cushion
Instamart moving to owned inventory from mid-Q3 FY27, which management says adds ~80 bps of contribution margin
risks: Instamart's adjusted EBITDA loss widened to ~₹895 Cr in Q2 FY27; contribution margin slipped to -1.0% of GOV
No. 3 in quick commerce behind Blinkit and Zepto by order share
Consolidated loss continues; the market has punished delays to breakeven
Rising competition from Flipkart Minutes and Amazon Now

zepto.name: Zepto
zepto.role: Unlisted pure-play quick-commerce app - No. 2 by orders - with 1,139 dark stores (Mar 2026)
strengths: Fastest order growth among scaled players; ~33% of the three leaders' orders in FY26 (its UDRHP)
Orders per store per day rising (2,140 in Q4 FY26) and ad income at 7.8% of order value
risks: FY26 restated loss of ₹5,905 Cr and negative free cash flow
IPO put on hold in late Jul 2026; a pre-IPO round was reported at ~US$4.5bn, down from US$7bn
notes: SEBI approved its IPO in May 2026; UDRHP-I filed 8 Jun 2026 (₹8,010 Cr fresh issue)
Listing reported for Feb-May 2027 - see the Zepto IPO deck
No listed market data

dmart.name: Avenue Supermarts (DMart)
dmart.role: India's most profitable large grocery retailer; DMart Ready is its online grocery arm with next-day and pick-up delivery
strengths: Lowest-cost store model in Indian retail sets the price benchmark quick commerce has to match
Owns most of its stores, so it can keep prices low through discount wars
DMart Ready gives an online option without dark-store losses
risks: Quick commerce is taking top-up grocery baskets from supermarkets in big cities
DMart Ready is small and slower than 10-minute apps
Store-growth pace and like-for-like growth have slowed in metros

flipkart.name: Flipkart
flipkart.role: Unlisted, Walmart-owned No. 1 e-commerce marketplace; also runs Flipkart Minutes (quick commerce), Ekart (logistics), Myntra and super.money (UPI)
strengths: Largest Indian marketplace by GMV, with its own logistics and fashion (Myntra)
Flipkart Minutes crossed ~800 dark stores by April 2026 and plans more
risks: Unlisted; deep discounting in quick commerce ahead of a planned listing
Foreign-owned, so it cannot hold inventory for Indian shoppers under FDI rules
notes: Majority-owned by Walmart; moved its holding company back to India in 2025 ahead of a planned IPO
No DRHP filed as of Oct 2026
No listed market data

amazonIndia.name: Amazon India
amazonIndia.role: Unlisted Indian arm of Amazon - No. 2 marketplace, Amazon Now (quick commerce), Amazon Pay and its own logistics
strengths: Parent's balance sheet and Prime membership
Amazon Now scaled to several hundred dark stores in 2026
risks: Unlisted; India losses absorbed by the parent
Same FDI inventory limits as Flipkart
notes: Wholly owned by Amazon.com Inc.
No listed market data

meesho.name: Meesho
meesho.role: Value e-commerce marketplace for tier-2/3 India with zero seller commission; earns from seller ads and logistics (Valmo)
strengths: 284 million annual transacting users (Q2 FY27, +21%) - the widest reach among Indian marketplaces
Contribution margin rose to 6.0% of NMV in Q2 FY27 and free cash flow turned positive
Valmo, its asset-light logistics network, keeps delivery costs low
risks: Order growth slowed to 17% in Q2 FY27 (sale timing shifted to Q3)
Still loss-making at the net level after listing in Dec 2025
Low-ticket orders leave little room if logistics or ad income falls

nykaa.name: FSN E-Commerce Ventures (Nykaa)
nykaa.role: Leading online and omnichannel beauty retailer (Nykaa) with a fashion marketplace (Nykaa Fashion) and own brands
strengths: Beauty is a high-margin, inventory-led category where authenticity matters, giving Nykaa pricing power
Guided ~30% GMV growth in Q2 FY27; 338 stores add omnichannel reach
Own brands (Kay Beauty, Dot & Key) lift gross margin
risks: Quick commerce selling beauty in 10 minutes threatens repeat purchases
Fashion is still a small, low-margin business
Competition from Tira (Reliance) and Myntra beauty

firstcry.name: Brainbees Solutions (FirstCry)
firstcry.role: India's largest specialty retailer of baby and kids' products - app, ~1,000+ stores, own brands, and GlobalBees D2C roll-up
strengths: Category leader with strong own brands (BabyHug) and an omnichannel network
Expanding in the Middle East (UAE, Saudi Arabia)
risks: Still loss-making at the net level; GlobalBees roll-up weighs on margins
Quick commerce and Meesho competing in diapers and basics

lenskart.name: Lenskart Solutions
lenskart.role: Digital-first eyewear brand: designs and makes its own frames and lenses and sells via app and ~3,500 stores in India and abroad
strengths: Vertically integrated (own factory in Rajasthan), so gross margins are above 70%
Q1 FY27 revenue rose ~43% with ~22% EBITDA margin; India same-store sales +18%
International business (Owndays, Middle East) was ~44% of revenue in Q1 FY27
risks: Store-led growth needs constant capex
Rich valuation since its Nov 2025 listing leaves little room for misses (see the figures)
Currency and execution risk abroad

yatra.name: Yatra Online
yatra.role: Online travel company focused on corporate travel (flights, hotels, MICE) for 1,000+ corporate customers
strengths: Largest corporate travel management platform among Indian OTAs - sticky B2B contracts
Hotels and MICE carry higher take rates than flights
risks: Small scale versus MakeMyTrip and ixigo
Corporate travel budgets are cyclical
US-listed parent's holding and past restructuring add complexity

ixigo.name: Le Travenues Technology (ixigo)
ixigo.role: Mass-market travel app - India's largest IRCTC partner for train tickets, plus flights, buses (AbhiBus) and hotels
strengths: Gross transaction value grew ~22% in Q2 FY27, with flights up ~37% and hotels up 2.6x
Strong Gen-Z and tier-2 user base built on trains
Profitable while investing in hotels and AI trip planning
risks: Train bookings depend on IRCTC's partner terms
Thin take rates on flights; airline consolidation
Rising marketing spend for hotels

easemytrip.name: Easy Trip Planners (EaseMyTrip)
easemytrip.role: Online travel agency built on flight bookings with no convenience fee, expanding into hotels and holidays
strengths: Low-cost, flight-led model that was profitable from early on
Debt-light balance sheet
risks: Promoter stake sales and governance questions in 2025
Flight bookings slowing; diversification acquisitions are unproven
Heavy dependence on air-ticket volumes

makemytrip.name: MakeMyTrip
makemytrip.role: India's largest online travel company (MakeMyTrip, Goibibo, redBus) - listed on Nasdaq, not in India
strengths: Leader in hotels and holidays, the high-commission end of online travel
Profitable with large cash reserves
risks: Not listed in India; Trip.com reduced its stake in 2025
Competition from ixigo in trains/buses and from direct airline bookings
notes: Listed on Nasdaq (MMYT); reported to have filed confidentially for an Indian listing in 2026 (unverified)
No NSE market data

irctc.name: IRCTC
irctc.role: Indian Railways' online ticketing monopoly; every rail-booking app (ixigo, Paytm, ConfirmTkt) sells through it
strengths: Statutory monopoly on online rail tickets earns convenience fees with no customer-acquisition cost
Partners pay IRCTC for access, so it gains whoever wins rail bookings
risks: Fee levels and revenue share are set by the Railways ministry
Travel apps own the customer interface; IRCTC's own app competes with its partners

infoEdge.name: Info Edge (India)
infoEdge.role: Owns Naukri (jobs), 99acres (property), Jeevansathi (matrimony) and Shiksha (education), plus stakes in Eternal and PB Fintech
strengths: Naukri is the dominant Indian job portal with operating margins above 50%
Collects subscriptions upfront, so cash flow is strong and the company is net-cash
Stakes in Eternal and PB Fintech give indirect exposure to food, quick commerce and insurance
risks: Naukri billings track IT-services hiring
Reported profit swings with investee fair values and write-downs
AI and LinkedIn changing recruitment

indiamart.name: IndiaMART InterMESH
indiamart.role: India's largest B2B marketplace - small businesses pay subscriptions to list products and get buyer leads
strengths: Dominant B2B listing platform with high operating margins and upfront subscriptions
Net-cash, with investments in SaaS (Busy accounting software)
risks: Paying-supplier growth has been slow; churn among smaller subscribers
Competition from WhatsApp-led discovery and ONDC

justdial.name: Just Dial
justdial.role: Local-search and listings platform for small businesses, majority-owned by Reliance Retail
strengths: Large paid-listing base of local businesses and a cash-rich balance sheet
Reliance parentage for B2B and JioMart tie-ups
risks: Search traffic increasingly goes to Google Maps and AI assistants
Slow growth in paid campaigns

cartrade.name: CarTrade Tech
cartrade.role: Auto classifieds (CarWale, BikeWale), OLX India and Shriram Automall (used-vehicle auctions)
strengths: Leading auto classifieds plus a physical auction network - earns from both dealers and buyers
OLX India (bought 2023) adds general classifieds
risks: Used-vehicle volumes tied to auto finance cycles
Competition from CarDekho, Spinny and Cars24

urbanCompany.name: Urban Company
urbanCompany.role: Marketplace for home services (beauty, cleaning, repairs) that trains and equips professionals; also sells Native water purifiers and smart locks
strengths: Clear leader in organised home services in India, with operations in the UAE and Saudi Arabia
Native products add a higher-margin hardware business
Listed in Sep 2025 with a strong cash position
risks: Gig-worker welfare rules and partner protests over commissions
New 'Insta Help' (15-minute household help) burns cash
Thin margins outside the core India business

nazara.name: Nazara Technologies
nazara.role: Listed gaming company: mobile and casual games (Kiddopia, Animal Jam, Fusebox), esports and ad tech; exited real-money gaming after the 2025 ban
strengths: The only scaled listed gaming company in India, with mostly global revenue
Esports and gaming IP benefit from the 2025 Act's recognition of esports
risks: Wrote down its stake in Moonshine (PokerBaazi) after the real-money ban - a ₹915 Cr charge in Q2 FY26 and more in Q1 FY27
Q1 FY27 net loss; founder Nitish Mittersain stepped down as CEO
Acquisition-led growth adds integration risk

physicsWallah.name: PhysicsWallah
physicsWallah.role: Low-cost online and offline test-prep (JEE, NEET, UPSC) built on a YouTube following; listed Nov 2025
strengths: Very low course prices and a large free audience keep acquisition costs low
Hybrid online-offline centres in smaller cities
risks: Offline expansion raises fixed costs and lowers margins
Test-prep demand is cyclical and competitive; AI tutors may reduce willingness to pay
The stock has traded well below its listing-day level

dream11.name: Dream11 (Dream Sports)
dream11.role: Unlisted former fantasy-sports leader; shut its real-money contests after the 2025 Act
strengths: Very large user base and IPL/sports brand recognition
risks: Shut its real-money contests in Aug 2025 when the ban passed; pivoting to free-to-play and other products
notes: Private (Dream Sports); shows the regulatory risk in this zone
No listed market data

delhivery.name: Delhivery
delhivery.role: India's largest independent e-commerce and freight logistics network; bought Ecom Express in 2025
strengths: Express parcel volume up ~32% in Q2 FY27 to ~325 million shipments as Ecom Express volumes moved in
Net profit in Q2 FY27 against a loss a year earlier, with Ecom Express integration costs largely behind it
Neutral network used by Meesho, D2C brands and marketplaces
risks: Price pressure from large shippers that also run captive fleets
Part-truckload freight is competitive and cyclical
Customer concentration among large marketplaces

shadowfax.name: Shadowfax Technologies
shadowfax.role: Last-mile and hyperlocal delivery network serving e-commerce, quick commerce and food apps; listed Jan 2026
strengths: Rider-led network suited to same-day and quick-commerce deliveries
Grows with Meesho, Flipkart and quick-commerce volumes
risks: Heavy dependence on a few large platforms
Low margins and gig-worker cost exposure
Listed below its issue price in Jan 2026

shiprocket.name: Shiprocket
shiprocket.role: Shipping and commerce-enablement software for small online sellers and D2C brands - books any courier, checkout, and fulfilment from one dashboard; listed Aug 2026
strengths: Asset-light: earns per shipment without owning trucks or riders
Large base of small D2C and social sellers outside the big marketplaces
risks: Merchants can go direct to couriers as they grow
Still building profitability at listing

blueDart.name: Blue Dart Express
blueDart.role: Premium express courier and air-cargo network (DHL group); carries higher-value e-commerce and B2B shipments
strengths: Own aircraft and the most reliable premium network in India
Parent DHL's global network for cross-border parcels
risks: E-commerce is a minority of revenue and price-sensitive
Margins hit by fuel and aircraft costs

paytm.name: One 97 Communications (Paytm)
paytm.role: Payments app, merchant soundboxes and card machines, payment gateway and loan distribution for partner lenders
strengths: Q2 FY27 profit rose ~10x to ~₹225 Cr; EBITDA margin crossed 10%
Revenue grew ~28% in Q2 FY27 and subscription merchants reached 1.64 crore
Largest merchant device base (soundboxes) in India
risks: The new UPI fee covers only merchant payments above ₹2,000, so most UPI volume still earns nothing
Loan distribution depends on partner lenders' appetite for unsecured credit
Regulatory history: the 2024 RBI order on Paytm Payments Bank

phonepe.name: PhonePe
phonepe.role: Unlisted, Walmart-owned No. 1 UPI app by volume, plus merchant QR, insurance, lending and Indus Appstore
strengths: Largest share of UPI transactions; scale advantage on merchant acceptance
risks: Unlisted; UPI market-share cap debate targets it directly
Monetisation outside UPI is still building
notes: Filed an updated DRHP (pure offer for sale) in Jan 2026; paused in Mar 2026; targeting a listing by Mar 2027 per reports
No listed market data

pineLabs.name: Pine Labs
pineLabs.role: Merchant payments and card-machine leader for large retailers and brands, with EMI and issuing software; listed Nov 2025
strengths: Leader in point-of-sale EMI for brands (electronics, appliances) - earns from brands and banks, not just per swipe
Growing issuing and gift-card software (Qwikcilver) in India and abroad
risks: Card-machine business faces UPI QR substitution
Turned profitable only recently; acquisition-heavy history

mobikwik.name: One MobiKwik Systems
mobikwik.role: Payments app and payment gateway (Zaakpay) with digital credit and wealth products; listed Dec 2024
strengths: Asset-light credit distribution to a mass user base
Payment-gateway business adds merchant revenue
risks: Small UPI share versus PhonePe, Google Pay and Paytm
Loss-making after listing as lending partners tightened
Exposed to RBI digital-lending rules

razorpay.name: Razorpay
razorpay.role: Unlisted leading online payment gateway for internet businesses and SMEs, plus payroll and banking software
strengths: Largest online gateway among startups and D2C brands
risks: Unlisted; payment-aggregator rules and fee-free small UPI payments limit margins
notes: Reported to have filed confidentially for an IPO in Jun 2026
No listed market data

affle.name: Affle 3i
affle.role: Mobile performance-advertising platform that charges per conversion (install, sign-up, purchase); India and emerging markets plus developed markets
strengths: Cost-per-converted-user model ties revenue to advertisers' results
Customers include Indian e-commerce, fintech, gaming and food apps
Consistently profitable with net cash
risks: Google/Apple privacy changes limit tracking
Real-money gaming ban removed a big Indian ad category
Ad-fraud and data-protection (DPDP Act) compliance

tanla.name: Tanla Platforms
tanla.role: Largest A2P SMS and business-messaging platform in India (OTPs, alerts), with the Trubloq anti-spam ledger and Wisely WhatsApp/RCS platforms
strengths: Scale in Indian enterprise messaging; anti-spam platform used by telecom operators
Net cash and steady dividends
risks: A2P SMS volumes are falling as traffic shifts to WhatsApp and RCS
Telecom operators set SMS prices
Platform revenue growth has been slower than hoped

routeMobile.name: Route Mobile
routeMobile.role: Global CPaaS (SMS, WhatsApp, RCS, voice) provider; majority-owned by Belgium's Proximus since 2024
strengths: Global reach and the Proximus group's carrier relationships
Debt-free after clearing borrowings in FY26; guiding mid-to-high single-digit growth for FY27
risks: FY26 revenue fell and profit dropped ~24% on vendor write-offs
A2P SMS softness and low gross margins

rategain.name: RateGain Travel Technologies
rategain.role: SaaS for hotels, airlines and car rentals: rate intelligence, channel distribution and marketing
strengths: Global hotel and travel customers; recurring SaaS revenue
Benefits from travel booking growth without inventory risk
risks: Most revenue is from the US and Europe, not India
Acquisition integration and slower growth in distribution

unicommerce.name: Unicommerce eSolutions
unicommerce.role: Order, warehouse and multi-channel software for online sellers and D2C brands, plus Shipway shipping; promoted by AceVector (the Snapdeal parent)
strengths: Used by thousands of sellers across marketplaces and quick commerce - grows with order volume
Profitable, debt-free SaaS
risks: Small scale; large brands may build in-house tools
Pricing pressure from Shiprocket and others

apple.name: Apple (India operations)
apple.role: The largest brand making phones in India - iPhones are assembled by Foxconn and Tata Electronics, mostly for export
strengths: iPhone exports reached about ₹2L Cr in FY26, India's single largest branded export (Business Today, Apr 2026)
Roughly one in four iPhones sold worldwide in 2025 was assembled in India
risks: Not listed in India; exposure only through its assemblers and suppliers
US trade policy and tariffs decide how much export volume stays in India
notes: Apple Inc. is listed in the US (NASDAQ: AAPL); its Indian subsidiaries are not listed
Its contract manufacturers, not Apple itself, would claim MPMS incentives

samsung.name: Samsung India Electronics
samsung.role: Runs one of the world's largest phone factories at Noida, making Galaxy phones for India and export
strengths: Plans to make Galaxy S26 flagships in Noida (Mar 2026)
Large enough to qualify for MPMS Track 1 on its own
risks: Not listed in India
Its earlier PLI benefits ended in FY25; future incentives depend on clearing MPMS growth hurdles
notes: Subsidiary of Samsung Electronics (Korea Exchange); not listed in India
Also outsources some models to Indian EMS firms such as Dixon

lava.name: Lava International
lava.role: India's main home-grown phone brand, the most likely candidate for MPMS Track 2 (Indian brands)
strengths: Indian-owned with in-house design - the profile Track 2 rewards with 5% plus 3% for design and R&D
CLSA named it the domestic brand most likely to benefit (Aug 2026)
risks: Small share of a market dominated by Chinese-linked brands, Samsung and Apple
IPO plans have been delayed repeatedly
notes: Unlisted; filed draft IPO papers in 2021, listing pushed to FY27 or later per reports
Track 2 needs ₹1,000 Cr FY26 turnover and passing a five-part Indian-brand test

redington.name: Redington
redington.role: Large IT and mobility distributor - distributes iPhones and other smartphones across India
strengths: Scale distributor with long-standing Apple relationship, so it benefits from rising India iPhone sales
Low valuation and dividend yield versus EMS stocks
risks: Distribution margins are thin (around 1-2% net)
Benefits from phone demand, not from MPMS incentives directly

moschip.name: MosChip Technologies
moschip.role: Hyderabad chip-design services company (ASIC, SoC, embedded) building its own product designs
strengths: One of very few listed Indian pure plays on chip design
Revenue rose from ₹148 Cr (FY22) to ₹585 Cr (FY26)
risks: Mostly services revenue; product bets are early
High valuation for a services business

lt.name: Larsen & Toubro
lt.role: L&T's wholly owned fabless chip unit (LTSCT): power, analog and silicon-carbide chips for autos, industry and energy
strengths: Showed 40 products including its first 1,200V silicon-carbide MOSFET at SEMICON India (Sep 2026)
Agreed with Tata Electronics (18 Sep 2026) to explore making and packaging its chips in India
L&T invested ₹542 Cr in the unit in FY26 (₹859 Cr cumulative)
risks: Tiny relative to L&T's ₹2.86L Cr revenue - no visible impact on the stock yet
Revenue target of US$500m by FY31 is ambitious and unproven

cyient.name: Cyient
cyient.role: Engineering services company that set up Cyient Semiconductors (Apr 2025) for custom chips (ASICs) and its own fabless products
strengths: 25+ years of ASIC work for industrial, data-centre, auto and medical clients
Aims to build India's first fabless chip product company (Investor Day, Aug 2026)
risks: Semiconductor unit is small inside a much larger engineering-services business
No disclosed product revenue milestones yet

tataProjects.name: Tata Projects
tataProjects.role: EPC contractor that built Micron's Sanand ATMP plant
strengths: Delivered India's first large chip-packaging plant for Micron (contract Sep 2023), a rare cleanroom track record in India
risks: Unlisted; no public market data
Construction margins are thin and project-dependent
notes: Tata group company; not listed
Tata Electronics separately signed Taiwan's Kelington for Dholera fab infrastructure (Sep 2026)

ionExchange.name: Ion Exchange (India)
ionExchange.role: Water-treatment company that makes ultra-pure water (UPW) and zero-discharge systems
strengths: Already supplies UPW systems for solar cell plants (₹205 Cr orders, Dec 2025) - the same technology fabs need
Recurring resin, chemical and service income after each installation
risks: No disclosed semiconductor UPW order yet
FY26 profit fell to ₹143 Cr on project-margin pressure

blueStar.name: Blue Star
strengths: Large project business that builds controlled-environment HVAC for factories and data centres
Strong balance sheet and execution record
risks: Semiconductor cleanrooms are a small niche in a consumer-AC-heavy business
Foreign cleanroom specialists compete for fab packages

thermax.name: Thermax
thermax.role: Utility systems: boilers, chillers, water treatment and captive power for industrial campuses
strengths: Supplies the heating, cooling and water utilities large plants need
Broad industrial customer base
risks: Chip-plant orders are not separately disclosed
Utility packages for fabs often go to specialist foreign vendors

dixon.name: Dixon Technologies
dixon.role: India's largest home-grown EMS company and biggest Indian phone assembler (Samsung, Motorola, Xiaomi, Vivo and others)
strengths: Brokerages (Macquarie, JPMorgan) call it the clearest MPMS beneficiary
Vivo JV approved (Jul 2026) adds a large anchor customer; ~₹1,100 Cr of phone exports in Q1 FY27
Building camera and display module plants that can earn part of the 1.5% sourcing bonus
risks: CLSA cut it to Underperform (Aug 2026): much of its sales may miss the hurdle unless exports grow
Kotak estimates MPMS adds only 0.14-0.22 percentage points to EBITDA margin
Thin margins and high customer concentration

foxconn.name: Foxconn India (incl. Bharat FIH)
foxconn.role: Foxconn group's Indian plants: its Tamil Nadu unit assembles most of India's iPhones, and Bharat FIH builds phones for other brands
strengths: The core iPhone export assembler; Bharat FIH is described as India's largest EMS provider
Bharat FIH has SEBI approval for a ~₹5,000 Cr IPO
risks: Not yet listed in India
Heavily dependent on Apple volumes and US trade policy
notes: Subsidiary of Hong Kong-listed FIH Mobile (Foxconn group)
IPO: ~₹5,004 Cr (half fresh issue, half offer for sale) - dates not announced as of Oct 2026

tataElectronics.name: Tata Electronics
tataElectronics.role: Tata group's electronics arm: iPhone assembly and casings, the Assam OSAT and the Dholera wafer fab with PSMC
strengths: The only company spanning phone assembly, chip packaging and a wafer fab in India
Assam OSAT began pilot production in Oct 2026 (planned 48 million chips a day)
Dholera fab (~₹91,000 Cr) partnered with PSMC and ASML
risks: Unlisted - no direct listed exposure
Fab commercial production now guided to mid-2028, later than first promised
notes: Wholly owned by Tata Sons; not listed
Bought Wistron's Indian iPhone plant (2023) and majority of Pegatron India (2025)
OSAT commercial production expected around Dec 2026-Jan 2027 (Assam Tribune)

optiemus.name: Optiemus Infracom
optiemus.role: Noida-based EMS company assembling smartphones (Ai+), wearables and IoT modules
strengths: Q1 FY27 revenue roughly doubled to ~₹883 Cr on a ~3 million-phone Ai+ programme
Added 6 million units of annual capacity (Noida Unit 3)
risks: EBITDA margin fell to 4.7% in Q1 FY27 as it built volume
Too small to enter MPMS Track 1 on its own - benefits through brand customers

amber.name: Amber Enterprises India
amber.role: Room-AC contract manufacturer entering smartphone assembly through a deal with Oppo, alongside its PCB and EMS units
strengths: Jun 2026 deal to make phones for Oppo, OnePlus and Realme: ~8 million units in year one, 15-16 million in year two
Macquarie called it a 'sleeper' MPMS beneficiary
risks: Trial production only in Q4 FY27, commercial in Q1 FY28 - no phone revenue yet
Profit fell to ₹226 Cr in FY26; heavy capex across PCBs and phones

syrma.name: Syrma SGS Technology
syrma.role: EMS and PCBA maker named by brokerages as a beneficiary of local component sourcing
strengths: Profit nearly doubled to ₹346 Cr in FY26 on 27% revenue growth
Kept as a top sector pick by brokerages after MPMS (Aug 2026)
risks: Phone-related revenue is a small share - most work is industrial, auto and consumer boards
Rich valuation

kaynes.name: Kaynes Technology India
kaynes.role: EMS company with India's second operating chip-packaging plant (Kaynes Semicon, Sanand) and PCB/camera-module projects under ECMS
strengths: Kaynes Semicon began commercial production in Mar 2026 (intelligent power modules for autos and industry)
Largest share of the first ECMS approvals (PCBs, camera modules, laminates)
Spans boards, components and chips - the full sourcing-bonus chain
risks: OSAT and ECMS plants are early and loss-making while they ramp
Heavy capex stretches the balance sheet
Stock has fallen sharply from its 52-week high

salcomp.name: Salcomp India
salcomp.role: Chennai-based maker of phone chargers and mechanics, a major supplier to Apple and Samsung
strengths: One of the largest charger makers in India, already supplying global phone brands
risks: Unlisted; no public market data
Owned by a Chinese group (Lingyi iTech), which shapes how it is treated in sourcing rules
notes: Subsidiary of Finland-origin Salcomp, owned by China's Lingyi iTech
Not listed in India

pgel.name: PG Electroplast
pgel.role: EMS company making room ACs, washing machines and plastic mouldings; mobile handsets are a small legacy line
strengths: Moulding and electronics capacity that could serve phone sub-assemblies
Rallied with the EMS group on MPMS approval (+4.6% on 16 Jul 2026)
risks: Phone revenue is small and not disclosed - room ACs drive results
FY26 profit fell to ₹197 Cr despite higher revenue

cyientDlm.name: Cyient DLM
cyientDlm.role: Hyderabad EMS company building circuit boards and boxes mainly for aerospace, defence, medical and industrial customers
strengths: Adds to India's domestic PCBA capacity; rose ~3% on the scheme approvals (16 Jul 2026)
risks: Little direct phone exposure - its customers are aerospace, medical and industrial
Revenue fell in FY26 (₹1,261 Cr vs ₹1,520 Cr) on deferred shipments

micron.name: Micron Semiconductor Technology India
micron.role: Memory-chip assembly and test (ATMP) plant at Sanand - India's first chip plant in commercial production
strengths: Commercial production since Feb 2026 (inaugurated by the PM)
Project cost ~₹22,516 Cr, built by Tata Projects
risks: Unlisted subsidiary of US-listed Micron
Memory is a highly cyclical market
notes: Subsidiary of Micron Technology (NASDAQ: MU); not listed in India

cgpower.name: CG Power and Industrial Solutions
cgpower.role: Power-equipment maker whose majority-owned CG Semi (with Renesas and Stars Microelectronics) runs a chip-packaging plant at Sanand
strengths: CG Semi's ₹7,600 Cr OSAT was inaugurated by the PM on 4 Jul 2026 - a listed, operating chip plant
Record FY26 revenue (₹12,418 Cr) from the core power-equipment business funds the ramp
risks: OSAT start-up losses weigh on group profit for several years
Very high valuation

hclFoxconn.name: India Chip (HCL-Foxconn JV)
hclFoxconn.role: HCL group and Foxconn joint venture building a display-driver chip packaging plant at Jewar, UP
strengths: Display-driver chips go into every phone, TV and laptop screen - a direct link to the MPMS supply chain
Foundation stone laid Feb 2026
risks: Unlisted; HCL group's stake is held by its promoter entity, not HCL Technologies
Pre-revenue
notes: Approved under Semicon 1.0 (~₹3,706 Cr)
Not listed

spel.name: SPEL Semiconductor
spel.role: Small Chennai chip-packaging company - the only long-standing listed OSAT
strengths: Decades of packaging know-how and a rare listed OSAT name
risks: Persistently loss-making with revenue under ₹10 Cr
Thin float; too small to bid for Semicon 2.0's ₹1,000 Cr minimum projects alone

archean.name: Archean Chemical Industries
archean.role: Marine-chemicals company (bromine, salt) whose subsidiary SiCSem is building India's first commercial silicon-carbide fab in Odisha
strengths: SiCSem (~₹2,066 Cr project) signed its fiscal-support agreement with ISM on 11 May 2026
Partner Clas-SiC (UK) brings SiC fab know-how; Archean invested GBP 15m in it
risks: Core chemical profits have fallen for three years (₹383 Cr FY23 to ₹105 Cr FY26)
SiCSem is pre-revenue and large relative to Archean's own size

glassSolutions.name: 3D Glass Solutions (HIPS)
glassSolutions.role: US company building a glass-substrate advanced-packaging unit in Bhubaneswar, Odisha
strengths: Glass substrates are an emerging technology for AI and RF chip packaging
Fiscal-support agreement Feb 2026, groundbreaking Apr 2026
risks: Unlisted; first-of-a-kind technology at commercial scale
notes: Approved Aug 2025 (~₹1,943 Cr); Indian unit: Heterogeneous Integration Packaging Solutions
Not listed

crystalMatrix.name: Crystal Matrix
crystalMatrix.role: Integrated gallium-nitride (GaN) compound-semiconductor and micro-LED display fab with packaging at Dholera
strengths: Approved by Cabinet in May 2026 as India's first GaN micro-LED display fab
risks: Unlisted and pre-construction; technology risk is high
notes: Approved with Suchi Semicon on 5 May 2026 (~₹3,936 Cr combined)
Not listed

psmc.name: Powerchip Semiconductor (PSMC)
psmc.role: Taiwanese foundry licensing process technology and training staff for Tata's Dholera fab
strengths: Brings mature-node foundry know-how India lacks
risks: Not listed in India; earns fees rather than owning the plant
notes: Listed in Taiwan; technology partner, not owner, of the Dholera fab

scl.name: Semi-Conductor Laboratory (SCL), Mohali
scl.role: Government-owned legacy fab for strategic chips (space, defence)
strengths: India's only long-running chip fab; makes strategic chips
risks: Old technology and small capacity; government-owned
notes: Under the Ministry of Electronics & IT; not listed

appliedMaterials.name: Applied Materials India
appliedMaterials.role: World's largest chip-equipment maker; large engineering centre in Bengaluru
strengths: Announced a US$5bn, 10-year India plan at SEMICON India 2026: a 140-acre research park and 10x local supply-chain capacity
risks: Not listed in India; benefits flow to its Indian suppliers
notes: Subsidiary of Applied Materials (NASDAQ: AMAT); not listed in India

lamResearch.name: Lam Research India
lamResearch.role: Etch and deposition toolmaker setting up its first Indian silicon-component plant
strengths: Committed ~₹10,000 Cr to India; already qualifies parts from Indian suppliers
risks: Not listed in India
notes: Subsidiary of Lam Research (NASDAQ: LRCX); not listed in India

asml.name: ASML
asml.role: Dutch maker of lithography scanners - partner to Tata Electronics' Dholera fab
strengths: Sole supplier of the most advanced lithography tools; partnership with Tata Electronics (May 2026)
risks: Not listed in India; export controls govern which tools can ship
notes: Listed in Amsterdam and on NASDAQ; not in India

asmtec.name: ASM Technologies
asmtec.role: Bengaluru engineering firm doing design and precision manufacturing for semiconductor-equipment makers; JV with Hind High Vacuum for tools
strengths: Long record of engineering services for semiconductor-equipment companies
Revenue nearly doubled to ₹529 Cr in FY26; profit ₹61 Cr
New plants at Dabaspet (Karnataka) and Sriperumbudur (Tamil Nadu)
risks: Very high valuation - priced well ahead of earnings
Small company dependent on a few global toolmaker clients

linde.name: Linde India
linde.role: Industrial-gas company building on-site gas supply for Tata's Dholera fab and a gas facility for Sanand's OSATs
strengths: Dholera air-separation plant for Tata's fab due in H2 2027
Acquired land in Sanand for an OSAT gas facility (2026)
Long take-or-pay contracts give utility-like visibility
risks: Chip gas revenue starts only as fabs ramp
Very high valuation

inoxAp.name: INOX Air Products
inoxAp.role: Industrial-gas company building an electronic specialty-gas hub at Dholera
strengths: ~₹500 Cr Dholera hub for ultra-high-purity gases; already supplies Gujarat's first chip plant
Makes about 12 semiconductor gases in India and plans 10 more
risks: Unlisted
Says 20-25 gases chips need may keep coming from imports
notes: JV of INOX group and Air Products (NYSE: APD); not listed

fluorochem.name: Gujarat Fluorochemicals
fluorochem.role: Fluorochemicals and fluoropolymers maker that set up a semiconductor-materials subsidiary in Jun 2026
strengths: New wholly owned GFCL Semiconductor and Advanced Materials Ltd (incorporated 26 Jun 2026)
Fluorine chemistry is the base of many etch and cleaning gases
risks: Semiconductor materials are at planning stage - no revenue
Core refrigerant and polymer margins are cyclical

navin.name: Navin Fluorine International
navin.role: Specialty fluorochemicals maker targeting electronic chemicals for semiconductors and batteries
strengths: Profit more than doubled to ₹664 Cr in FY26
Has named electronic chemicals as a future business segment
risks: Semiconductor revenue not yet disclosed
High valuation leaves little room for delays

lt.name: Larsen & Toubro
lt.role: Bidder for the magnet scheme (Aug 2026); also building EV traction motors with Israel's EVR Motors
strengths: Engineering and project-execution depth to build a first-of-its-kind plant
Captive demand: its EPS Mobility unit reported an order for 500,000 two-wheeler traction motors over three years (Autocar Pro, 30 Jul 2026)
risks: No prior rare-earth or magnet track record; reported to need a technology partner
A 600-1,200 tonne magnet unit would be tiny next to L&T's revenue - no earnings impact for years

coalIndia.name: Coal India
coalIndia.role: The most active PSU in critical minerals: magnet-scheme bidder, winner of auction blocks at home and chasing lithium and copper in Chile
