strengths: Cash-rich balance sheet (net profit ₹31,071 Cr in FY26) can fund a plant without strain
Won a graphite-vanadium block in Chhattisgarh in the May 2025 auction round
Applied with Wealth Minerals' Chilean unit (Kuska) for a lithium operating contract and weighed buying the unit; also planning a Singapore minerals trading office (Reuters, Aug 2026)
PSU status may help with IREL oxide access and state support
risks: No magnet, rare-earth or lithium operating experience
The Chile deal waits on a Chilean licence; overseas diversification has produced little so far
Immaterial to Coal India's earnings even if it all works - the stock trades on coal volumes and dividends

microns20.name: 20 Microns
microns20.role: Industrial minerals maker that bid for the magnet scheme - the only small-cap listed bidder
strengths: If it wins, up to ₹645-1,290 Cr of incentives over five years would be large against FY26 revenue of ₹954 Cr
Mineral processing and micronising know-how
risks: No sintered-magnet experience disclosed; bid details are not public
Building an integrated plant could strain a small company's balance sheet
Highly binary: losing the bid leaves no rare-earth story

mam.name: Midwest Advanced Materials
mam.role: Building a private sintered NdFeB magnet plant in Hyderabad (500 tonnes a year first phase) - the closest to India's first commercial sintered-magnet output - with in-house oxide-to-metal and alloy steps; bid for the scheme as a Midwest Energy-MAM joint venture
strengths: Furthest along: technology from the government's NFTDC and Technology Development Board funding (PIB, May 2024); reported in Sep 2026 to be close to commercial output
Targets 5,000 tonnes a year (by 2030 per PIB, 2024; later reports say end-2027)
risks: Unlisted; listed Midwest Ltd is a sister concern, not its parent, so there is no clean listed route in
Commercial output dates have slipped (first magnets were targeted for Dec 2025)
notes: Hyderabad-based; part of the Midwest group (Kollareddy family)
Joint bid with Midwest Energy Ltd under the REPM scheme (PIB bidder list, 13 Aug 2026)
No public market data - not listed

proterial.name: Proterial (India)
proterial.role: Indian arm of Japan's Proterial (formerly Hitachi Metals), a global sintered-magnet maker; scheme bidder
strengths: Decades of sintered NdFeB know-how - one of few bidders that has made these magnets at scale
risks: Unlisted subsidiary of a privately held Japanese group - no Indian listed exposure
Bloomberg reported a consortium with two unnamed Indian automakers, but the official bidder list names only Proterial (India)
notes: Subsidiary of Proterial Ltd, Japan (formerly Hitachi Metals)
Named in the REPM bidder list (PIB, 13 Aug 2026)
No Indian market data - not listed

neo.name: NEO Performance Materials
neo.role: Canadian rare-earth magnet and materials group that bid through its Singapore unit
strengths: Runs rare-earth separation and magnet operations outside China, including a new sintered-magnet plant in Estonia
risks: Listed in Toronto, not in India - no Indian-listed exposure
Would likely need an Indian partner for oxide and approvals
notes: Bid via NEO Performance Materials (Singapore) Pte Ltd (PIB bidder list, 13 Aug 2026)
Listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange, not in India

attero.name: Attero Recycling
attero.role: E-waste and lithium-ion battery recycler that recovers lithium, cobalt, nickel and copper and is scaling rare-earth recovery; magnet-scheme bidder
strengths: Announced (June 2025) a ₹100 Cr plan to scale rare-earth recycling from 300 to 30,000 tonnes of feed a year
Existing e-waste collection network gives access to magnet scrap
risks: Unlisted (has said it plans an IPO) - no audited public financials here
Recovered volumes are small until EV motors reach end of life
notes: Noida-based e-waste and lithium-ion battery recycler
Named in the REPM bidder list (PIB, 13 Aug 2026)
No public market data - not listed

lohum.name: Lohum
lohum.role: Lithium-ion battery recycler and battery-materials maker, also building an NdFeB magnet plant in Uttar Pradesh; magnet-scheme bidder (Lohum Magnets & Energy Solutions)
strengths: Combines recycling and magnet making, so it can feed its own plant with recovered rare earths
risks: Unlisted - no audited public financials
Reported plant size and investment differ between announcements (₹500-3,000 Cr; 2,000-5,000 tonnes)
notes: Greater Noida-based critical-minerals recycler
ECMS approved its ₹700 Cr rare-earth magnet project (30 Mar 2026), billed by MeitY as India's first magnet plant starting from rare-earth oxides; not yet producing as of Oct 2026
Named in the REPM bidder list (PIB, 13 Aug 2026)
No public market data - not listed

irel.name: IREL (India) Ltd
irel.role: State-owned miner and processor of beach-sand minerals and India's only large rare-earth separator; supplies NdPr oxide to the three lowest scheme bidders
strengths: Holds the monazite: beach-sand plants in Kerala, Tamil Nadu and Odisha, rare-earth extraction in Odisha and separation at Aluva (Kerala)
Policy anchor of the whole chain - the scheme's 500-tonne oxide allocation runs through it
risks: Not investable: a fully government-owned company under the Department of Atomic Energy
Output is small - roughly 400-500 tonnes of neodymium a year (Reuters, Aug 2025)
notes: Central PSU under the Department of Atomic Energy
NdPr oxide capacity 400 tonnes a year plus about 500 tonnes of stock (REPM notification, Dec 2025)
No public market data - not listed

toyotsu.name: Toyotsu Rare Earths India
toyotsu.role: Toyota Tsusho unit that processes IREL rare-earth material in India, historically for export to Japan
strengths: Working separation operation with Japanese process know-how; IREL approached it in 2025 to help bring Japanese magnet makers to India
risks: Unlisted subsidiary of a Japanese trading house
Reuters reported (June 2025) that IREL was asked to suspend its rare-earth export arrangement with Japan to keep material at home, which would affect this business
notes: Subsidiary of Toyota Tsusho Corporation, Japan
No Indian market data - not listed

nftdc.name: Non-Ferrous Materials Technology Development Centre (NFTDC)
nftdc.role: Government R&D centre in Hyderabad that developed the magnet and alloy technology licensed to Midwest
strengths: One of the few Indian holders of rare-earth metal, alloy and magnet process know-how
risks: A research body, not a manufacturer - it enables others rather than earning from volumes
notes: Autonomous R&D centre under the Ministry of Mines
Technology partner for the Midwest magnet project and the Midwest-Indonesia MoU (2026)
Not a company - no market data

kmml.name: Kerala Minerals and Metals (KMML)
kmml.role: Kerala state-owned beach-sand miner making ilmenite, rutile and titanium dioxide
strengths: Operates on the Chavara coast, one of India's richest heavy-mineral sand belts
risks: Unlisted state company; rare earths are not its product - monazite goes to IREL
notes: Kerala state public sector company
Titanium-minerals focus; listed here for the beach-sand belt it mines
No public market data - not listed

midwestLtd.name: Midwest Ltd
midwestLtd.role: Granite and quartz miner with heavy-mineral-sand exploration licences in Sri Lanka; sister concern of the Midwest magnet venture
strengths: Holds four heavy-mineral-sand exploration licences in Sri Lanka, with operations targeted for FY27 pending environmental clearance (company website) - a possible non-Indian monazite source
Group link to India's furthest-advanced private magnet project
risks: Revenue today is black granite and quartz - rare earths are not yet a business line
The magnet plant sits in sister group entities (Midwest Energy / MAM), not under the listed company

gmdc.name: Gujarat Mineral Development Corporation (GMDC)
gmdc.role: Gujarat state miner developing the Ambadungar rare-earth deposit with BARC technology
strengths: Received BARC's indigenous rare-earth process technology for Ambadungar (19 Jan 2026)
Non-binding MoU with NMDC (16 Mar 2026) to study a full Gujarat rare-earth chain
risks: Rare earths are pre-revenue; earnings come from lignite and other minerals
Stock rallied on the theme and then fell back over the past year - sentiment-driven

nmdc.name: NMDC
nmdc.role: India's largest iron-ore miner, partnering GMDC on rare earths and looking for lithium abroad
strengths: Mining scale and cash flows to fund exploration
MoU with GMDC (Mar 2026) on Ambadungar
Said in 2025 it was evaluating critical-mineral acquisitions in Australia, Africa and South America; its Australian unit Legacy Iron Ore has a lithium exploration pact with Hancock Prospecting (2023)
risks: Rare earths are an MoU-stage side project next to ₹32,000 Cr of iron-ore revenue
No overseas lithium acquisition had been signed by Nov 2026

hindalco.name: Hindalco Industries
hindalco.role: Aditya Birla aluminium and copper major; runs India's largest custom copper smelter at Dahej (Gujarat) and is building e-waste and copper recycling
strengths: Adding 300,000 tonnes a year of copper smelting at Dahej, on track for FY29 - which the company says will make it the largest copper smelting site outside China
E-waste and copper recycling plants planned at Dahej and under construction at Pakhajan
Commissioned a battery-foil plant in Odisha in Jan 2026 (see the PLI-ACC battery policy)
risks: Custom smelters earn processing fees, which a global concentrate shortage has squeezed close to zero
Copper and recycling are smaller earnings drivers than aluminium and Novelis

hindcopper.name: Hindustan Copper
hindcopper.role: State-owned and India's only vertically integrated copper miner; 30% partner in KABIL
strengths: Plans to lift ore capacity from about 4.2 to 12.2 million tonnes a year by FY30, with about ₹7,189 Cr of capex (company, 2026)
The closest listed pure play on copper prices, which hit a record in Sep 2026
risks: FY26 ore output was 3.67 million tonnes - tripling it is a large execution task, and Indian mine expansions often slip
Earnings swing with the copper price; most of India's copper still comes from imported concentrate

vedanta.name: Vedanta
vedanta.role: After its 1 May 2026 demerger the parent keeps base metals - zinc and silver through Hindustan Zinc, plus copper (Silvassa refinery) - and bids actively for critical-mineral blocks
strengths: Won the Genjana nickel, chromium and PGE block (Dec 2025) and other blocks in earlier tranches - one of the most active private winners
Controls Hindustan Zinc, the other big group winner in the auctions
risks: Its Thoothukudi copper smelter has stayed shut since 2018 (closure upheld by the Supreme Court in Feb 2024), so copper is a small refining business today
Group debt and the demerger's moving parts make the critical-minerals piece hard to value

hindzinc.name: Hindustan Zinc
hindzinc.role: Vedanta's zinc, lead and silver miner, diversifying into critical minerals through block auctions
strengths: Won tungsten blocks in Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu (Nov 2024), a rare-earth block in Uttar Pradesh and potash-halite blocks in Rajasthan in later rounds; got a letter of intent for the Gundlupet rare-earth and yttrium block in Karnataka (Sep 2026)
Underground mining know-how and strong cash flows to fund exploration
risks: The new blocks are at exploration stage - years from revenue
Zinc and silver prices, not critical minerals, drive earnings

adanient.name: Adani Enterprises
adanient.role: Group incubator whose Kutch Copper unit runs a greenfield copper smelter and refinery at Mundra
strengths: Phase 1 (0.5 million tonnes a year of refined copper) shipped first cathodes in Mar 2024; the company targets 1 million tonnes a year by FY29
Port-side site suits imported concentrate
risks: Copper is one of many businesses inside a diversified, capex-heavy group
Concentrate sourcing and ramp-up at the group's first metals plant

gravita.name: Gravita India
gravita.role: Listed recycler of lead, aluminium and plastics that started a 6,000-tonne-a-year lithium-ion battery recycling plant at Mundra (Jan 2026)
strengths: Existing scrap-collection network in India and abroad - the hardest part of battery recycling
The pilot makes black mass; extracting lithium, nickel, cobalt and manganese - what the recycling scheme pays for - is planned for about FY29, and a copper recycling plant at Mandvi is also planned
risks: Management called the lithium unit a pilot with no significant near-term revenue (Q4 FY26 call, May 2026)
Lead recycling still drives earnings; no recycling-scheme award has been disclosed

nalco.name: National Aluminium Company (NALCO)
nalco.role: State alumina and aluminium maker; KABIL's largest shareholder (40%)
strengths: A listed, if very indirect, route into KABIL's overseas lithium and cobalt bets
risks: KABIL is tiny next to NALCO's alumina and aluminium business, which drives earnings

oilIndia.name: Oil India
oilIndia.role: Upstream oil and gas PSU that has won a graphite-vanadium block in Arunachal Pradesh (Nov 2024)
strengths: Graphite is a battery anode input (anode makers sit in the PLI-ACC battery policy), so the block fits India's battery push
risks: Minerals are immaterial next to oil and gas
The block is at exploration stage

kabil.name: Khanij Bidesh India Ltd (KABIL)
kabil.role: Joint venture of NALCO (40%), Hindustan Copper (30%) and MECL (30%), set up in 2019 to buy critical-mineral assets abroad
strengths: Holds five lithium brine blocks (about 15,703 hectares) in Catamarca, Argentina, signed with state miner CAMYEN in Jan 2024 with a budget of about US$24 million
Works with Australia's Critical Minerals Office on lithium and cobalt projects
risks: Unlisted - investors get it only through NALCO and Hindustan Copper
Exploration stage: reports put first lithium output around 2029 at the earliest
notes: Joint venture of three central PSUs under the Ministry of Mines
Argentina environmental clearance for exploration was reported in Apr 2026 (not confirmed by an official release)
No public market data - not listed

maiki.name: Maiki South Mining
maiki.role: Kolkata-based private miner that won the Katghora lithium and rare-earth block in Chhattisgarh - the first domestic lithium block auctioned (2024)
strengths: Won with a 76.05% premium of mineral value, showing appetite for small domestic lithium blocks
risks: Private and unlisted; no disclosure of exploration progress
A high premium squeezes the economics if grades disappoint
notes: Preferred bidder for Katghora (Korba district) in the first critical-mineral tranche
No public market data - not listed

mecl.name: Mineral Exploration and Consultancy Ltd (MECL)
mecl.role: Ministry of Mines' exploration PSU that drills and prepares many of the blocks the Centre auctions; 30% KABIL partner
strengths: Central to the Mission's 1,200-project exploration push alongside the Geological Survey of India
risks: Unlisted - it enables the auctions rather than earning from mining
notes: Central PSU under the Ministry of Mines
No public market data - not listed

sona.name: Sona BLW Precision Forgings
sona.role: Sona Comstar: EV traction motors and driveline maker - among India's largest importers of rare-earth magnets
strengths: Restored April-level motor output by July 2025 despite China's curbs, using its own engineering
Has validated rare-earth-free ferrite-assisted motors for three-wheelers and light commercial vehicles
risks: Imported about 120 tonnes of magnets from China in a year (company, 2025) - the most exposed Indian motor maker to a new curb
Benefit from Indian magnets only arrives once scheme plants run, likely 2028 or later

unominda.name: UNO Minda
unominda.role: Makes traction motors for e-two- and three-wheelers (Uno Minda Buehler Motor) and EV powertrain electronics (a JV with China's Inovance) - a direct magnet buyer
strengths: Took full ownership of its EV-motor joint venture (approved Dec 2025), so it controls motor design and magnet sourcing
Reuters reported (Jul 2025) it explored local magnet production with Mahindra, which Mahindra denied - a sign the industry wants a domestic source
risks: No magnet-making plan of its own has been confirmed
Customers are concentrated in the price-competitive e-two-wheeler segment

bharatforge.name: Bharat Forge
bharatforge.role: Forgings major whose Kalyani Powertrain arm develops EV motors and inverters
strengths: Engineering base to localise e-motors as Indian magnet supply appears
risks: EV motors are a very small part of a forgings and defence business

bajaj.name: Bajaj Auto
bajaj.role: Two- and three-wheeler maker; its Chetak e-scooter was the biggest casualty of the 2025 magnet shortage
strengths: Cash-rich and highly profitable, able to hold buffer stocks and qualify new suppliers
Showed it could restart within weeks once magnets arrived (late Aug 2025)
risks: Chetak production fell 47% year on year in July 2025 (10,824 units) on magnet shortages
Still dependent on Chinese magnets until Indian plants run

tvs.name: TVS Motor
tvs.role: Two-wheeler maker whose iQube e-scooter depends on rare-earth hub motors
strengths: Kept iQube production up 6% year on year in July 2025 (23,742 units) while Bajaj's Chetak fell 47%
Reported, though not confirmed by the company, to be working on ferrite motors that cut rare-earth use
risks: Still dependent on imported magnets until Indian plants run (about 2028 at the earliest)
A ferrite switch would lower long-run demand for the magnets the scheme pays for

ola.name: Ola Electric
ola.role: E-scooter maker that certified an in-house rare-earth-free ferrite motor in Oct 2025
strengths: First Indian two-wheeler maker with a government-certified ferrite motor (7 kW and 11 kW variants)
Said its production was not hit by the 2025 magnet shortage
risks: Loss-making every year shown; revenue fell to ₹2,253 Cr in FY26
A ferrite motor is a substitute for, not a buyer of, the scheme's magnets

suzlon.name: Suzlon Energy
suzlon.role: India's largest wind-turbine maker; its S144 platform uses a doubly-fed induction generator (DFIG)
strengths: DFIG design means little exposure to rare-earth magnet shortages
risks: Low magnet content also means little direct gain from the scheme - easy to overstate the link
Wind orders depend on auctions and transmission

inoxwind.name: Inox Wind
inoxwind.role: Wind-turbine maker; its DF-series turbines use doubly-fed induction generators (DFIG), which need little rare-earth magnet
strengths: Little exposure to magnet shortages in today's geared DFIG designs
Would gain a local source if it moves to larger permanent-magnet machines
risks: Low magnet content means little direct gain from the scheme
Execution and working-capital history

bel.name: Bharat Electronics
bel.role: Defence electronics major (radars, EW, missile subsystems) - a small, strategic magnet user
strengths: Indigenisation push favours domestic magnet supply for radars, motors and microwave tubes
risks: Magnet use is not disclosed and is tiny next to revenue - an inferred, low exposure

bdl.name: Bharat Dynamics
bdl.role: Missile maker - fin actuators and seekers use rare-earth magnets (inferred from how these parts are built; not disclosed)
strengths: Secure domestic magnet supply supports missile indigenisation
risks: Exposure is inferred, not disclosed, and very small in value

hal.name: Hindustan Aeronautics
hal.role: Fighter, trainer and helicopter maker - control-surface actuators and generators use rare-earth (often samarium-cobalt) magnets
strengths: Long programmes (Tejas, helicopters) benefit from local strategic materials
risks: Magnet content is a negligible share of costs; low direct exposure

hal.name: Hindustan Aeronautics
hal.role: India's main aircraft and helicopter maker and the default production agency for DAC-approved aircraft (Tejas, Su-30, ALH, Prachand)
strengths: Order book of ₹2.54L Cr at 31 Mar 2026 - about 7-8 years of revenue
7 Sep 2026 DAC approved more Advanced Light Helicopters, its own product
Repair and overhaul of a large fleet gives steady revenue
risks: Engine supply limits deliveries: GE sent 6 of 11 promised F404 engines in FY26
FY27 revenue growth guided at only ~10-12% despite the orders
Fighter work-share on the 114-jet MRFA deal is not yet settled

bel.name: Bharat Electronics
bel.role: Main production agency for radars, EW, air-defence systems (Akash, QRSAM) and military communications
strengths: Order book ₹72,258 Cr (1 Jul 2026) and FY27 inflow guidance of >₹55,000 Cr
Makes the DRDO-designed Arudhra radar the Navy got approval for on 7 Sep 2026
Guides ~28% EBITDA margin and 15% revenue growth for FY27
risks: ~₹30,000 Cr QRSAM order awaited Cabinet approval as of Oct 2026; Q1 FY27 inflow fell ~49%
Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin dipped to ~25% on product mix
Large-cap valuation already prices strong execution

bdl.name: Bharat Dynamics
bdl.role: Government-owned missile maker - Akash, Astra, anti-tank missiles, MRSAM and torpedoes
strengths: Order book ~₹26,000 Cr (May 2026, broker estimate)
July 2026 DAC approvals (MPATGM, MRSAM, V-SHORADS) fall in its product range
Won a ₹1,348 Cr order from HAL for HELINA launchers (Jun 2026)
risks: FY26 revenue fell to ~₹2,440 Cr as supply-chain issues slowed execution
Astra revenue ramps only from Q3 FY27 and carries high import content
Rich valuation on depressed earnings

mazdock.name: Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders
mazdock.role: Builds destroyers and submarines; preferred yard for the P75(I) submarine programme with Germany's TKMS
strengths: P75(I) (~₹70,000 Cr, six submarines) cleared by the Finance Ministry and sent to the CCS (2026)
Only listed yard with a submarine franchise
Strong profit growth and high returns on equity
risks: P75(I) still unsigned as of Oct 2026; first boat ~7 years after signing
Order book (~₹18,000 Cr reported) is thin until big contracts land
Valuation assumes the big orders arrive

grse.name: Garden Reach Shipbuilders & Engineers
grse.role: Kolkata yard building frigates (P17A), anti-submarine shallow-water craft and export vessels
strengths: Revenue grew ~4x FY22-FY26 with the highest returns of the PSU yards
Positioned for next-generation corvettes and patrol vessels
Growing commercial and export shipbuilding
risks: Needs new large Navy orders as current programmes deliver
Fixed-price contracts expose margins to cost overruns
Smaller balance sheet than Mazagon or Cochin

cochin.name: Cochin Shipyard
cochin.role: Built INS Vikrant; builds anti-submarine craft and runs India's largest ship-repair business
strengths: Only Indian yard to have built an aircraft carrier - first in line for any second carrier
Ship repair gives steady, higher-margin revenue
Large commercial and export order book
risks: Defence is only part of revenue; commercial orders carry lower margins
FY26 profit fell ~13% year on year
A second carrier is not yet approved

lt.name: Larsen & Toubro
lt.role: Largest private defence prime: K9 Vajra guns, warships, Sarvatra bridging sub-systems and missile/aerospace parts
strengths: Won 100 more K9 Vajra-T guns for ₹7,629 Cr (Dec 2024), >80% indigenous work content
Builds warships at Kattupalli and supports BEML on the Sarvatra bridge (in the Sep 2026 AoN)
Huge balance sheet to fund private Make projects
risks: Defence is a small share of a ~₹2.9L Cr revenue group
Many defence wins depend on foreign design partners
Lumpy order timing

beml.name: BEML
beml.role: State-controlled maker of Army trucks, recovery vehicles and the Sarvatra mobile bridge; also mining and rail
strengths: Prime manufacturer of the Sarvatra bridge, re-approved by the DAC on 7 Sep 2026
High-mobility vehicles and mine layers in the same AoN fit its range
Diversified across defence, mining and metro rail
risks: FY26 profit roughly halved and ROE is low
Defence orders are tender-based and lumpy
Rail and mining cycles add volatility

bharatforge.name: Bharat Forge
bharatforge.role: Private artillery, armoured vehicle and ammunition maker through Kalyani Strategic Systems (KSSL)
strengths: Defence order book ₹11,196 Cr (end Q1 FY27); defence revenue +87.5% YoY in Q1 FY27
60% share of the ~₹6,900 Cr ATAGS gun order
KSSL EBITDA margin rose to 17.2% (Q1 FY27); exports of artillery and shells
risks: Defence is still a minority of a mostly auto-forging business
ATAGS revenue waits on remaining approvals
Q1 FY27 group loss from a one-off German restructuring charge

solar.name: Solar Industries India
solar.role: Largest private explosives maker - Pinaka rockets, ammunition, loitering munitions and missile propellants
strengths: Defence revenue ~doubled to ₹2,634 Cr in FY26 (27% of sales); FY27 guide ~₹4,500 Cr
Defence order book ~₹18,000 Cr of ₹21,350 Cr total (30 Jun 2026)
Owns its explosives chain, from raw material to finished rocket
risks: Pinaka is a large share of the defence book - single-programme risk
Very rich valuation (see the figures)
Explosives plants carry safety and licensing risk

premier.name: Premier Explosives
premier.role: Small maker of propellants, explosives and pyrotechnic devices for missiles, rockets and chaff/flares
strengths: Qualified supplier of solid propellants to DRDO and missile programmes
Defence share rising as ammunition orders grow
Revenue roughly doubled FY22-FY26
risks: Small company - one plant incident or order slip moves results
FY26 revenue dipped despite strong demand
High P/E for its size

datapatterns.name: Data Patterns (India)
datapatterns.role: Design-led defence electronics: radars, EW, avionics and processors sold to BEL, HAL and DRDO
strengths: Order book ₹928 Cr firm, ₹2,654 Cr incl. negotiated (30 Jun 2026)
Won a ₹586 Cr radar-electronics order from BEL (2026)
FY27 guide: 20-25% revenue growth and ~₹2,000 Cr of new orders
risks: Q1 FY27 profit fell ~13% - lumpy execution
Depends on BEL/HAL programme timing
New composites acquisition is unproven

astra.name: Astra Microwave Products
astra.role: RF and microwave sub-systems for radars, EW and missiles; partner on the Uttam fighter radar
strengths: Largest-ever order from HAL for Uttam AESA radar sub-systems (2026)
Consolidated order book ~₹4,300 Cr after that order
Long-standing DRDO/BEL supplier across radar programmes
risks: Q1 FY27 revenue fell ~11%
Orders depend on a few programmes and on BEL/HAL timing
Working-capital heavy

apollo.name: Apollo Micro Systems
apollo.role: Embedded electronics for missiles, torpedoes and drones; moving up to sub-system integration
strengths: Revenue grew ~3.7x FY22-FY26 as missile programmes ramped
Content on several DRDO missile and torpedo programmes
Expanding into larger sub-systems and integration
risks: High valuation on a small profit base
Receivables and inventory heavy
Depends on BDL/BEL production schedules

paras.name: Paras Defence and Space Technologies
paras.role: Defence optics (thermal imagers, sights, space optics), anti-drone systems and electronics
strengths: Optics and anti-drone are both on import-ban lists and in demand
Revenue up ~2.6x FY22-FY26 with improving profit
Space-optics niche adds a second growth leg
risks: Rich valuation leaves no room for slips
Small order sizes and lumpy revenue
Competes with much larger BEL in some products

avantel.name: Avantel
avantel.role: Software-defined radios and satellite-communication terminals for the Navy and other forces
strengths: Niche maker of naval satcom and SDR equipment
Secure communications are part of 2026 approvals (DEFSAC)
Debt-light and design-led
risks: FY26 profit fell sharply (to ~₹15 Cr) on lower revenue
Very high P/E on depressed earnings
Navy-concentrated order book

zen.name: Zen Technologies
zen.role: Combat training simulators and counter-drone systems for all three services
strengths: Order book ₹1,239 Cr (30 Jun 2026) plus a ₹177.5 Cr simulator order in July
Counter-drone systems are a post-Sindoor priority (₹289 Cr upgrade order, Oct 2025)
Targets 35% EBITDA margin in FY27
risks: Revenue fell ~29% in FY26 and ~10% in Q1 FY27 - orders are lumpy
Many counter-drone competitors, incl. BEL
Valuation built on a rebound

ideaforge.name: ideaForge Technology
ideaforge.role: Surveillance drones (SWITCH, ZOLT) for the Army and paramilitary
strengths: Won >₹100 Cr in emergency procurement (EP-6) orders after Operation Sindoor
Drones passed electronic-warfare and country-of-origin checks
Long incumbency with the Army
risks: Loss-making in FY25 and FY26
Revenue swings with a few tenders
Component supply constraints flagged by management

midhani.name: Mishra Dhatu Nigam (MIDHANI)
midhani.role: Government-owned maker of superalloys, titanium alloys and armour for aero engines, missiles and space
strengths: Only domestic source for many qualified defence superalloys
Engine and missile localisation increases demand
Armour products for vehicles and personnel
risks: Profit is below FY22 levels despite higher revenue
Slow execution and inventory build-up
Valuation assumes a turnaround

ptc.name: PTC Industries
ptc.role: Titanium and superalloy castings and forgings for aero engines, missiles and artillery
strengths: 2026 orders from BrahMos Aerospace (airframe) and Gun Factory Kanpur (artillery parts)
Building India's own titanium and superalloy melting capacity
FY26 revenue nearly doubled
risks: Priced far ahead of earnings - one of the richest valuations in the group
Large capex still ramping
Qualification timelines with global engine makers

azad.name: Azad Engineering
azad.role: Precision turbine and aero-engine parts for global engine makers and Indian defence programmes
strengths: Qualified on aero-engine and turbine parts for global OEMs
Engine localisation in India (marine gas turbines, fighter engines) widens its market
Revenue and profit growing ~30%+ a year
risks: Most revenue is not Indian defence - this is an indirect exposure
Very rich valuation (see the figures)
Customer concentration

ashok.name: Ashok Leyland
ashok.role: Truck maker that supplies the Army's logistics trucks and specialist vehicle chassis
strengths: Long-time supplier of Army logistics trucks
High-mobility vehicles were in the 7 Sep 2026 AoN
Large, profitable truck business funds defence bids
risks: Defence is a small share of a ~₹56,000 Cr revenue company
Truck tenders are price-competitive
Results driven by the commercial-vehicle cycle, not defence

tasl.name: Tata Advanced Systems
tasl.role: Tata group's defence arm: C-295 aircraft final assembly, ATAGS guns (with Bharat Forge), wheeled armoured platforms
strengths: Runs India's first private military aircraft final-assembly line (C-295, Vadodara)
40% share of the ATAGS gun order
Tata group balance sheet
risks: Unlisted - only reachable through Tata group holding companies
Many programmes are with foreign partners
notes: Wholly owned by Tata Sons
No separate listed equity
Figures not shown - not listed

aweil.name: Advanced Weapons & Equipment India
aweil.role: Government-owned gun and small-arms maker formed from the ordnance factories (Dhanush artillery)
strengths: Makes the Dhanush 155 mm gun, reported in the 27 Mar 2026 AoN round
Legacy gun factories and barrel know-how
risks: Unlisted DPSU
History of slow execution at the old ordnance factories
notes: One of seven DPSUs carved out of the Ordnance Factory Board in Oct 2021
100% government-owned
Not listed

munitions.name: Munitions India
munitions.role: Government-owned ammunition maker (former ordnance factories) - largest producer of shells, rockets and explosives
strengths: India's largest ammunition producer
Shares the Pinaka rocket contract with Solar Industries
risks: Unlisted DPSU
Capacity and quality issues inherited from the old ordnance factories
notes: One of seven DPSUs carved out of the Ordnance Factory Board in Oct 2021
100% government-owned
Not listed

dixon.name: Dixon Technologies
dixon.role: India's largest EMS company (phones, TVs, appliances) using ECMS to move into camera modules, display modules and optical transceivers through JVs with Chinese partners
strengths: Several ECMS approvals: camera modules via Kunshan Q Tech India and optical transceivers via Dixon Electroconnect (Jan 2026), display modules via Dixon Display Technologies (Mar 2026, ₹1,100 Cr)
Display JV with China's HKC received Press Note 3 approval on 9 Mar 2026
Scale: FY26 revenue ~₹48,900 Cr gives it captive demand for its own modules
risks: Depends on Chinese partners (HKC, Q Tech) for technology and on government approvals for each JV
Very thin assembly margins (net margin ~3%) until components scale
Phone volumes concentrated in a few brands

kaynes.name: Kaynes Technology India
kaynes.role: High-mix EMS (industrial, auto, aerospace, meters) building India's broadest ECMS footprint: HDI and multi-layer PCBs, laminate and camera modules in Tamil Nadu
strengths: First-tranche approvals (Oct 2025) for four Kaynes Circuits projects worth ₹3,280 Cr: HDI PCB (₹1,684 Cr), copper-clad laminate (₹1,167 Cr), camera modules (₹325 Cr) and multi-layer PCB (₹104 Cr)
Chennai PCB plant described as close to going live in Aug 2026
Higher-margin industrial and aerospace book than phone-focused peers
risks: Q4 FY26 profit fell ~21% and Q1 FY27 profit ~24% YoY despite 40% revenue growth
Kotak flagged accounting and disclosure issues in Dec 2025 (company disputed them); stock fell sharply
Heavy, simultaneous capex in PCBs, laminate and an OSAT plant

syrma.name: Syrma SGS Technology
syrma.role: EMS company (industrial, auto, consumer, healthcare) adding a multi-layer and HDI PCB fab in Andhra Pradesh with Korea's Shinhyup, plus camera modules
strengths: First-tranche approval for a ₹765 Cr multi-layer PCB unit (Syrma Strategic Electronics, Naidupeta, AP); construction began Dec 2025
Further approvals: camera modules via Syrma Mobility (Nov 2025), a ₹385 Cr project (Mar 2026) and coils (Aug 2026)
Andhra Pradesh cleared an ~₹856 Cr state incentive package for the PCB plant
risks: PCB plant commissioning guided for late 2026/FY27 - not yet producing
JV structure with a Korean partner for know-how
Stretched valuation (see the figures)

amber.name: Amber Enterprises India
amber.role: Room-AC contract manufacturer turning into an electronics group: IL JIN (EMS) and Ascent Circuits (PCBs), now building multi-layer and HDI board plants
strengths: Ascent Circuits got a ₹991 Cr multi-layer PCB approval (Oct 2025) for Hosur, with trial production guided for Q2 FY27 (Jul-Sep 2026)
Ascent-K Circuit (JV with Korea Circuit) got ECMS approval for a ₹3,200 Cr HDI/flex PCB plant near Jewar (Jan 2026); groundbreaking Jun 2026
Cooperation pact with Germany's Schweizer Electronic (Jun 2026) for auto/industrial boards
risks: Earnings still dominated by seasonal room-AC business; FY26 profit fell to ₹226 Cr
₹4,200 Cr of PCB capex before meaningful PCB revenue
Commissioning delays flagged by brokers

cyientdlm.name: Cyient DLM
cyientdlm.role: Design-led EMS for aerospace, defence, medical and industrial customers - a buyer of the high-reliability boards ECMS fabs will make
strengths: High-reliability customers (aerospace, defence) value local board supply and traceability
Design-to-build capability raises stickiness
risks: No ECMS approval of its own found as of Oct 2026 - an indirect beneficiary
FY26 revenue fell ~17% on aerospace order timing
Thin ROE

avalon.name: Avalon Technologies
avalon.role: EMS for US and Indian industrial, clean-energy, mobility and medical customers, with in-house cable, sheet-metal and PCB assembly
strengths: US-heavy industrial customer base wants non-China supply chains
FY26 revenue up ~46% to ₹1,603 Cr
risks: No ECMS approval found as of Oct 2026 - indirect beneficiary through cheaper local boards
Customer concentration in a few US accounts

unominda.name: UNO Minda
unominda.role: Auto-component major (lighting, switches, sensors, EV electronics) adding automotive camera modules
strengths: Listed among the Nov 2025 tranche's camera-module approvals (per India Briefing's list)
Captive demand from Indian carmakers' ADAS and reversing cameras
risks: Camera modules are a small part of a ~₹19,700 Cr auto business
Auto cameras face global Tier-1 competition

mindacorp.name: Minda Corporation
mindacorp.role: Spark Minda group auto-electronics supplier whose subsidiary Minda Instruments makes instrument clusters and is adding TFT display modules
strengths: Minda Instruments approved for display module sub-assembly (Aug 2026) - a greenfield TFT module plant in Pune
Backward integration into displays for its own digital clusters
risks: Small plant (~₹270 Cr reported) relative to the group
Automotive display volumes are far smaller than phones

motherson.name: Samvardhana Motherson International
motherson.role: Global auto-components group building precision enclosures for phones and IT hardware through Motherson Electronic Components
strengths: ECMS approval (Jan 2026) for enclosures for mobile and IT hardware
Kanchipuram enclosure plant due to start around Oct-Nov 2026 (reported Aug 2026)
Global precision-manufacturing scale and balance sheet
risks: Electronics is a tiny share of a ~₹1.26L Cr auto business
Enclosure customers are few and demanding

hindalco.name: Hindalco Industries
hindalco.role: Aditya Birla Group's aluminium and copper major, approved to make aluminium extrusions for mobile phone enclosures
strengths: Jan 2026 approval for aluminium extrusion for phone enclosures - previously fully imported
Integrated from bauxite to alloy, so it can supply consistent phone-grade alloy
risks: The ECMS project is immaterial to a ~₹2.75L Cr group; the stock moves with aluminium prices and Novelis
Phone-housing alloys need lengthy brand qualification

jyoticnc.name: Jyoti CNC Automation
jyoticnc.role: Rajkot machine-tool maker (CNC turning and machining centres) - the largest ECMS capital-equipment approval
strengths: ₹1,021 Cr ECMS approval for capital goods (Aug 2026)
Enclosure plants need thousands of machining centres - a large local demand pool
High ROCE and profit up ~2x since FY24
risks: Must match Japanese/Taiwanese machines on precision and uptime for electronics
Lumpy orders and working capital typical of machine tools
Rich valuation

asmtec.name: ASM Technologies
asmtec.role: Engineering-services and design-led manufacturing company approved to make high-precision capital equipment
strengths: ECMS approval in Mar 2026 for ₹565 Cr of high-precision capital equipment
Design-led manufacturing expansion at Dabaspet and Sriperumbudur
risks: Approved investment is large relative to its ~₹530 Cr revenue
Very high valuation - priced well ahead of earnings

srf.name: SRF
srf.role: Chemicals and films major supplying capacitor-grade polypropylene film, the dielectric inside film capacitors
strengths: First-tranche ECMS approval (Oct 2025, ₹496 Cr) for polypropylene film in Madhya Pradesh
Commissioned phase 1 of its capacitor-grade BOPP film line at Indore (~₹277 Cr) in May 2026
Strong balance sheet and fluorochemicals cash flows
risks: Capacitor film is a small part of a ~₹15,800 Cr business
Deferred a separate ₹490 Cr BOPP packaging-film project (May 2026) on weak film pricing

pcbl.name: PCBL Chemical
pcbl.role: India's largest carbon-black maker, approved to make acetylene black - the conductive additive in Li-ion battery electrodes
strengths: ECMS approval (Aug 2026) for an ~₹329 Cr acetylene black project - a first for India
Existing carbon-black scale, customers and process know-how
risks: FY26 profit fell ~55% to ₹198 Cr; battery materials are tiny vs tyre-grade carbon black
Timeline, capacity and location not yet disclosed

acutaas.name: Acutaas Chemicals
acutaas.role: Gujarat specialty chemicals company (pharma intermediates, CDMO) with a fast-growing battery-electrolyte-additives business
strengths: ECMS approval (17 Aug 2026) for its electrolyte additives plant at Jhagadia: ₹119 Cr eligible investment, incentive up to 25% through FY31
Battery chemicals already in commercial supply (per PL, Jul 2026)
High ROCE and FY26 profit more than doubled
risks: Valuation already prices in battery growth
Battery-chemicals demand depends on global cell makers' qualification cycles

bpl.name: BPL
bpl.role: Old consumer-electronics brand that now mainly makes printed circuit boards for lighting and automotive customers
strengths: Approved in the Jan 2026 tranche for PCB manufacturing
Existing PCB plant and customers

ECMS approvals in the Nov 2025 and Jan 2026 tranches

mitsubishiElec.name: Mitsubishi Electric India
mitsubishiElec.role: Indian arm of Mitsubishi Electric, approved in Aug 2026 (₹99 Cr) to make capital goods

risks: Unlisted; small approved investment

ola.name: Ola Electric Mobility
ola.role: Electric-scooter maker and PLI-ACC's largest awardee (20 GWh) - the only awardee with a running cell line, at its Krishnagiri gigafactory in Tamil Nadu, using cells in its own scooters

Captive demand from its own scooters

New targets of 12 GWh by Jul 2027 and 20 GWh by end-FY28 are far above today's running capacity
Loss-making scooter business funds the cell plant; market share has fallen

reliance.name: Reliance Industries
reliance.role: Conglomerate building a battery and BESS gigafactory at Jamnagar through Reliance New Energy Battery - 15 GWh of PLI-ACC awards (5 GWh in 2022, 10 GWh re-bid signed Feb 2025)
strengths: 49th AGM (2026): a 40 GWh first phase on track for commissioning in 2026 with all equipment on site; long-term target raised to 120 GWh a year of LFP cells and BESS
Captive demand: its Kutch renewable hub plans up to 150 MWh of battery containers a day at peak installation
Balance sheet to fund the plant without the incentive
risks: No PLI-qualifying capacity commissioned yet; penalties of about ₹5 lakh a day accrued from the missed 2024 milestone
Management has said access to Chinese battery technology is being 'weaponised'
Battery business is tiny relative to oil-to-chemicals, Jio and retail

rajeshexpo.name: Rajesh Exports
rajeshexpo.role: Bengaluru gold refiner and jeweller (owner of Swiss refiner Valcambi) whose subsidiary ACC Energy Storage won a 5 GWh PLI-ACC award for a plant in Karnataka
strengths: Holds a 5 GWh PLI-ACC award (programme agreement Jul 2022; tripartite pact with the Centre and Karnataka, Jan 2023)

Least progress of the awardees: about 19 months of delay in getting land possession (reported late 2025) and no cell line
Penalties of about ₹5 lakh a day accrued from the missed 2024 milestone
No battery experience; the stock reflects the gold business, not cells

exide.name: Exide Industries
exide.role: India's largest lead-acid battery maker, building a 12 GWh lithium-ion cell plant at Devanahalli near Bengaluru through Exide Energy Solutions - without a PLI-ACC award - plus Li-ion packs
strengths: Phase I (6 GWh) commissioned on 23 Sep 2026 - the second sizeable cell plant in India after Ola's
MoU with Hyundai and Kia (Apr 2024) to localise LFP cells for their India EVs
Brand, distribution and lead-acid cash flows fund the build-out
risks: Commissioning came after its own end-FY26 target; has flagged delays on its LFP line
Technology licensed from China's SVOLT
Must win third-party cell orders to fill the plant

amararaja.name: Amara Raja Energy & Mobility
amararaja.role: No. 2 lead-acid battery maker building a lithium cell 'Giga Corridor' in Telangana through Amara Raja Advanced Cell Technologies, plus a BESS assembly plant
strengths: Customer qualification plant commissioned Jul 2026; 2 GWh NMC cells due Q2 CY2027, scaling to 16 GWh (NMC and LFP) by FY30
10 GWh BESS assembly plant due Q3 FY27
~₹1,900 Cr already invested; plans to bid for the 10 GWh grid-storage PLI tender (Aug 2026)
risks: Lost earlier PLI-ACC bids
Its tie-up with China's Gotion collapsed; developing technology in-house
Large capex before cell revenue

agratas.name: Agratas Energy Storage Solutions
agratas.role: Tata Group's battery-cell company, building a 20 GWh first phase at Sanand, Gujarat (and a gigafactory in Somerset, UK) - not a PLI-ACC awardee
strengths: Sanand steel frame completed Apr 2026; production expected in 2027
NMC cells on licensed Japanese technology due early 2027; building its own LFP pilot line (Aug 2026 report)
Anchor customers in Tata Motors' passenger EVs and JLR
risks: Unlisted; no public financials
Two chemistries and two countries at once
Depends on Tata EV volumes
notes: Wholly owned by Tata Sons (unlisted) - not a Tata Motors subsidiary
Closest listed exposure: Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles (TMPV), its anchor customer, shown in this policy
No listed market data

waaree.name: Waaree Energies
waaree.role: India's largest solar-module maker moving into batteries through Waaree Energy Storage Solutions: BESS containers now, lithium cells next
strengths: 5.15 GWh BESS container plant commissioned Jul 2026
3.5-4 GWh cell line being set up (targeted for around Dec 2026) and a ₹8,175 Cr, 16 GWh integrated plant announced in Andhra Pradesh (Feb 2026)
Raised ₹1,003 Cr for the storage subsidiary (Jan 2026); bid in the 2024 PLI re-tender
risks: Storage is small next to modules; cell technology partner not disclosed
BESS containers compete with complete Chinese imports
Solar-module cycle drives the stock

kabra.name: Kabra Extrusiontechnik
kabra.role: Plastic-extrusion machinery maker whose Battrixx division assembles lithium-ion packs and BMS for electric two- and three-wheelers
strengths: One of the larger independent EV pack makers for two- and three-wheelers
In-house BMS design
risks: Small company; pack margins are thin and set by vehicle makers
Customer concentration in a few EV makers
All cells imported

tataautocomp.name: Tata AutoComp Systems
tataautocomp.role: Tata group auto-components maker assembling EV battery packs through Tata AutoComp Gotion, a JV with China's Gotion High-Tech
strengths: Supplies packs to Tata Motors' EVs and others
Global cell-maker partner
risks: Unlisted
Chinese partner subject to Press Note 3 scrutiny
notes: Held by Tata Sons and Tata Industries (unlisted)
No listed market data

adanigreen.name: Adani Green Energy
adanigreen.role: Renewable developer running India's largest BESS at its Khavda renewable park in Gujarat
strengths: 3.37 GWh of BESS commissioned at Khavda (incl. 1.37 GWh added Mar 2026) - the largest single-location BESS outside China, per the company
Targets over 10 GWh more storage in FY27
Storage firms up its solar for evening supply
risks: Cells and containers imported
High leverage and group-level governance scrutiny
Storage economics depend on merchant and contracted tariffs

acme.name: ACME Solar Holdings
acme.role: Renewable developer focused on firm and peak-power (FDRE) contracts that bundle solar with large battery storage
strengths: 4.96 GWh of BESS operational by Oct 2026 after adding ~437 MWh in Rajasthan
25-year PPAs with central renewable agencies for FDRE and assured-peak projects
Bid in the 2024 PLI-ACC re-tender (not awarded)
risks: Imported cells; exposed to cell-price and duty swings
Execution of several storage-heavy projects at once
Leverage

jswenergy.name: JSW Energy
jswenergy.role: Power producer with a 5 GWh battery assembly plant in Pune and a growing BESS and pumped-storage book
strengths: Locked-in storage of 29.6 GWh: 26.4 GWh pumped hydro and 3.2 GWh BESS (mid-2026)
Won a 200 MW/400 MWh BESS supply order from Bondada (Jul 2026)
Targets 40 GWh of storage by 2030

Storage is a small part of a thermal-plus-renewables business

indigrid.name: IndiGrid Infrastructure Trust
indigrid.role: KKR-backed power-transmission InvIT that now owns standalone battery storage, contracted on long-term fixed payments

180 MW/360 MWh Gujarat BESS (awarded 2024) commissioned May 2026

Tight tariffs in competitive BESS auctions
Imported cells

ntpc.name: NTPC

tatapower.name: Tata Power
tatapower.role: Integrated utility building storage as an EPC contractor and developer, plus large pumped hydro

1,000 MW/6,000 MWh Bhivpuri pumped storage fast-tracked by CEA

Group cell bet sits in Agratas (Tata Sons), not Tata Power

tmpv.name: Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles

Customer qualifications abroad and at home

risks: Commercial production only targeted for early 2028
New technology for a packaging company; needs cell-maker approval

Timelines at the Jamnagar giga complex have slipped before
Captive electrolyser technology still being proven at scale

Hydrogen is tiny next to L&T's infrastructure, defence and IT businesses

adaniEnt.name: Adani Enterprises (Adani New Industries)

Very large capex on top of its renewables build-out
Hydrogen returns are unproven versus its core power business

Higher cost per tonne until hydrogen prices fall
Steel cycle drives capex decisions

tataSteel.name: Tata Steel

No commercial green hydrogen supply contract found as of Oct 2026
European operations absorb decarbonisation capex

sail.name: Steel Authority of India (SAIL)

Large blast-furnace base where hydrogen injection could scale
risks: Pilot scale only - no commercial supply contract
PSU capex priorities sit with capacity expansion

ioc.name: Indian Oil Corporation
ioc.role: India's largest refiner and the first to contract green hydrogen supply (Panipat)

Among the four refiners with SIGHT Mode 2B allocations
Panipat's expansion creates a large new hydrogen need
risks: Tender had to be re-run twice before it drew bids
Green hydrogen costs well above its own grey hydrogen
Volumes are small versus total refinery use

bpcl.name: Bharat Petroleum

Only winner of SIGHT Tranche I's biomass bucket (2,000 tonnes a year, Jan 2024)
Refinery Mode 2B allocation for its own plants
risks: Thin returns at ₹279/kg if costs overrun
Green hydrogen is immaterial to refining and marketing earnings
Execution in Assam (land, power)

hpcl.name: Hindustan Petroleum
hpcl.role: State refiner contracting green hydrogen for its Visakh refinery
strengths: Visakh tender (5,000 tonnes a year, floated Oct 2024) reportedly won by Ocior Energy at ₹328/kg ex-GST
Among the refiners with SIGHT Mode 2B allocations
risks: Small volume relative to refinery needs
Depends on an unlisted developer's execution

gail.name: GAIL (India)
gail.role: Gas pipeline and city-gas group running its own 10 MW green hydrogen plant and owning the network that could carry hydrogen blends
strengths: Commissioned a 10 MW PEM electrolyser at Vijaipur, MP in May 2024 (~4.3 tonnes a day), used captively
India's largest gas pipeline network - the natural carrier for hydrogen blending
risks: Hydrogen is a tiny part of a gas transmission and marketing business
Blending limits and pipeline-steel compatibility still being studied

paradeep.name: Paradeep Phosphates
paradeep.role: Phosphate fertiliser maker in Odisha and Goa - the buyer in SECI's first green ammonia auction
strengths: First SECI green ammonia auction (Jul 2025): 75,000 tonnes a year from ACME at ₹55.75/kg, a 10-year fixed price
Replaces imported ammonia, a volatile dollar-priced input
Paradip port location suits a green hydrogen hub
risks: Fixed price may look high if imported ammonia gets cheap
Supply start depends on ACME's plant being built
Fertiliser subsidy and pricing are government-set

coromandel.name: Coromandel International
coromandel.role: Murugappa group fertiliser maker (Kakinada, Vizag) contracting green ammonia under SECI's auctions
strengths: ACME won a 50,000-tonne-a-year green ammonia round for Coromandel at ₹51.89/kg (Aug 2025)
Large ammonia importer, so a fixed rupee price reduces input swings
risks: Green ammonia is a small share of its raw material for years
Depends on developers' timelines

gnfc.name: Gujarat Narmada Valley Fertilizers & Chemicals
gnfc.role: Gujarat state-backed fertiliser and chemicals maker contracting green ammonia for Bharuch
strengths: SECI auction (Aug 2025): 50,000 tonnes a year from Onix Renewable at ₹52.50/kg
Ammonia feeds both its fertiliser and chemicals lines
risks: Supplier is a smaller unlisted developer
Chemicals cycle drives earnings far more than green ammonia

waaree.name: Waaree Energies
waaree.role: Solar-module major whose subsidiary Waaree Clean Energy Solutions won both electrolyser and green hydrogen production incentives
strengths: 300 MW a year electrolyser manufacturing award - the largest in Tranche II (Aug 2024)
90,000 tonnes a year green hydrogen production award (Tranche II, Mar 2025)
Can pair hydrogen with its own solar modules and storage
risks: No electrolyser factory commissioning confirmed as of Oct 2026
Hydrogen is tiny next to its module business
Technology partner and stack design not widely disclosed

advait.name: Advait Energy Transitions
advait.role: Small power-transmission products and EPC company turning into an electrolyser maker - the purest listed SIGHT electrolyser bet
strengths: Electrolyser awards in both tranches: 100 MW (Jan 2024, with Rajesh Power Services) and 200 MW (Aug 2024)
Hydrogen is material to its size, unlike the conglomerates
risks: Small balance sheet for a capital-heavy, technology-heavy business
Stack technology and customers still to be proven
Highly sensitive to delays in producer orders

thermax.name: Thermax
thermax.role: Energy and environment engineering group (boilers, heat exchangers, water treatment) offering complete alkaline electrolyser systems under a HydrogenPro licence
strengths: Aug 2025 licence and supply deal with Norway's HydrogenPro: exclusive in India, with Thermax making the balance of plant
Said it expects domestic electrolyser demand from around mid-2026 and planned to be ready by then (Feb 2026)
Already sells water treatment, heat recovery and utilities to refineries and fertiliser plants
risks: Stacks are bought from the licensor, so margins are shared
Hydrogen orders still small and lumpy
Competes with integrated foreign packagers

ionExchange.name: Ion Exchange (India)
ionExchange.role: Water-treatment specialist whose ultra-pure water systems are the kind every electrolyser needs
strengths: Builds ultra-pure water and effluent systems for refineries, power and industry
Won ~₹205 Cr of ultra-pure and waste-water orders in Dec 2025
risks: No hydrogen-specific order found as of Oct 2026 - an indirect beneficiary
Hydrogen projects' water packages are small per plant

inoxIndia.name: Inox India (INOXCVA)
inoxIndia.role: Cryogenic tank and equipment maker (LNG, industrial gases, liquid hydrogen) at Kandla and other plants
strengths: Built India's largest liquid hydrogen tank (238 m³) for Air Liquide's Korean project, shipped from Kandla in Aug 2022
Kandla plant sits beside the Deendayal green hydrogen hub
Existing LNG and industrial-gas customers overlap with hydrogen users
risks: Most hydrogen exports will move as ammonia, which needs different tanks
Hydrogen orders are occasional, not a steady stream

adaniGreen.name: Adani Green Energy
adaniGreen.role: Adani group's listed renewable developer, the natural power supplier to the group's planned Mundra hydrogen hub
strengths: Very large solar and wind build-out at Khavda, Gujarat
Group captive demand from Adani New Industries
risks: No hydrogen power supply contract disclosed as of Oct 2026
Leverage and group governance scrutiny

acmeSolar.name: ACME Solar Holdings
acmeSolar.role: Listed renewable producer of the ACME group; the group's green ammonia projects sit in the unlisted parent ACME Cleantech, not here
strengths: Experience in round-the-clock (FDRE) and storage-linked renewables - the kind of power hydrogen plants need
Sister company of India's largest green ammonia auction winner
risks: No disclosed power supply to ACME's ammonia projects
Investors may confuse it with the unlisted parent's hydrogen pipeline

adaniPorts.name: Adani Ports and SEZ
adaniPorts.role: India's largest private port operator; Mundra sits next to the group's planned green hydrogen and ammonia hub
strengths: Owns the port beside Adani New Industries' Mundra project
Liquid and gas handling experience
risks: Green ammonia exports are years away and small next to its cargo base
None of the three official hydrogen hub ports is an Adani port

amGreen.name: AM Green
amGreen.role: Green ammonia developer founded by Greenko's founders, building a 1 million-tonne-a-year first phase at Kakinada, Andhra Pradesh
strengths: Kakinada construction started Jan 2026; plans 7.5 GW of renewables, 2 GW of pumped storage and ~1.95 GW of electrolysers (1.3 GW ordered from John Cockerill)
Export offtake with Uniper (up to 5 lakh tonnes a year, Jan 2026), JERA, Yara, and Germany's H2Global Asian lot (≥€585m over 10 years, Sep 2026)
90,000 tonnes a year SIGHT production award (Mar 2025)
risks: Unlisted - no public financials
First production has slipped from late 2026 towards 2027
Very large capex concentrated in one site
notes: Privately held (AM Green group, linked to Greenko)
Electrolysers from John Cockerill Greenko Hydrogen Solutions, which also holds a SIGHT manufacturing award
No listed market data

acmeCleantech.name: ACME Cleantech Solutions
acmeCleantech.role: Unlisted parent of the ACME group and the largest winner of SECI's green ammonia auctions; building export ammonia at Gopalpur, Odisha
strengths: Six SECI green ammonia contracts, over 3.5 lakh tonnes a year, including the record-low ₹49.75/kg for IFFCO Paradeep
90,000 tonnes a year SIGHT production award (Jan 2024)
Long-term supply pact with Japan's IHI for ~4 lakh tonnes a year (signed Jan 2024), certified for Japan's CfD support in Jul 2026
risks: Unlisted - no public financials
Many projects at once across Odisha and other states
Very low bid prices leave little room for cost overruns
notes: Parent of listed ACME Solar Holdings (ACMESOLAR), which holds the renewable power business
No listed market data for the hydrogen projects

ohmium.name: Ohmium
ohmium.role: US-headquartered PEM electrolyser maker with a factory in Bengaluru
strengths: Electrolyser awards in both tranches (137 MW each, Jan and Aug 2024)
One of the few makers already producing stacks in India
risks: Unlisted; depends on venture funding
PEM costs more than alkaline per MW
notes: Privately held (Ohmium International, US)
No listed market data

iffco.name: IFFCO (Indian Farmers Fertiliser Cooperative)
iffco.role: India's largest fertiliser cooperative; its Paradeep and Kandla plants are among the biggest green ammonia buyers
strengths: Contracted the lowest green ammonia price yet: 1 lakh tonnes a year at ₹49.75/kg from ACME for Paradeep
Kandla: 1 lakh tonnes a year from ACME at ₹54.73/kg (SECI's eighth green ammonia auction)
risks: Cooperative - not listed
Supply depends on ACME's build
notes: Farmer-owned cooperative, not listed
No listed market data

nrl.name: Numaligarh Refinery
nrl.role: Assam refinery that ran India's lowest-priced refinery green hydrogen tender
strengths: Awarded 10,000 tonnes a year to BPCL-Sembcorp JV NeuEN at ₹279/kg (Feb 2026), target 2028
risks: Unlisted; small volume
notes: Majority-owned by Oil India (NSE: OIL)
No listed market data

deendayal.name: Deendayal Port Authority (Kandla)
deendayal.role: Major Gujarat port recognised as a green hydrogen hub (Oct 2025)
strengths: Hub status brings priority land and shared infrastructure for hydrogen and ammonia projects
Large land bank on the Gulf of Kutch
risks: Government port authority - not listed
Hub status carries no direct cash support
notes: Central government port authority
No listed market data

paradipPort.name: Paradip Port Authority
paradipPort.role: Odisha port recognised as a green hydrogen hub (Oct 2025), close to ACME's and fertiliser makers' plants
strengths: Near Paradeep Phosphates and IFFCO Paradeep, both green ammonia buyers
East-coast route to Japan and Korea
risks: Government port authority - not listed
Hub status carries no direct cash support
notes: Central government port authority
No listed market data
